description: Deciduous herb to 0.4 m tall. Subterranean stem a subglobose tuber, to 5 cm across and 3 cm high, tan outside, with offsets on mature specimens. Pseudostem to 10 by 1 cm, green. Leaf solitary; cataphylls to 10 cm long, pale carmine; petiole to 25 by 3–10 mm at base, pale olive-green to mid-green, with a brown hue at the base; leaf blade trifoliolate; leaflets broadly elliptic-ovate, to 18 by 12 cm, margins entire, apex acuminate, ending in a short arista 1 cm long, baseconvex; central leaflet with a petiolule to 4 cm long; lateral leaflets slightly asymmetrical, with a petiolule ca 1 cm long, glossy bluish green with impressed veins above, paler with slightly raised veins beneath. Inflorescence emerging as the leaf unfolds, more or less held at foliage level; peduncle slightly shorter than the petiole, 2.5–4 mm wide, same as colour of petiole; spathe tube subcylindrical, widening at the top, with a distinct, slightly expanded, white annulus at the base, to 2.5 by ca 1.5 cm, pale yellow-green; spathe mouth margins yellow-green and widely recurved; spathe limb broadly ovate, longer than the tube, 5–7 by ca 1.5 cm wide, outside pale green, and inside with a paler spot in the middle lower face, apex long acuminate; spadix appendix protruding from the tube but shorter than the spathe, erect, ending in a brush of yellow-green, upright fleshy bristles, these 4 by 0.5 mm; lower part sessile; pistillate spadices with appendix ca 3.5 cm long by 4 mm across at the base, the middle part thickened and naked, the lower 1 cm with scattered, white, curved projections, ca 2 mm long; staminate spadices with appendix shorter, ca 1.7 cm long, with bristles topping the staminate flowers, without any naked zone; fertile zone staminate or pistillate; staminate flower zone ca 2 by 0.5 cm; staminate flowers densely packed in the upper part, loosely arranged below, sessile or subsessile, 1–3-androus; anthers orange-brown; thecae dehiscing by an elongate pore; pistillate flower zone subcylindrical, 1.5 cm long by 7–8 mm across; pistillate flowers densely packed; ovaries ovoid, glossy dark green, each ovary containing ca 4 ovules; stigma on a short style, penicillate. Infructescence not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Arisaema sizemoreae . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 210. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Deciduous herb to 0.8 m tall. Subterranean stem a subglobose tuber, up to 7 cm across by 4 cm high, cream. Pseudostem 30–40 by 1.5 cm at the base, pink, brown mottled. Leaf solitary; cataphylls to 20 cm long, pink and brown mottled; petiole to 40 by 1 cm, red-brown or olive-green with transverse paler mottling; leaf blade radiate; leaflets 11–14, elliptic, 20–30 by 3–4 cm, margins flat or undulate, green or reddish, apex acuminate, ending in a carmine thread to 9 cm long, base cuneate, sessile to subsessile, shiny green, with slightly impressed veins above, underside glaucous with slightly prominent red-brown or green veins. Inflorescence carried below the foliage; peduncle 3–17 cm long by 4–5 mm across, green with paler mottling, becoming reddish towards the inflorescence; spathe tube funnel-shaped, 7–8 by 1.2–1.5 cm at the base and 3–4.5 cm above, outside pruinose, dark red-brown or pale olive-green with thin, white stripes, inside pale red-brown with white stripes; spathe mouth margins straight, red-brown; spathe limb ovate, horizontal, 9–10 by 5–6 cm, outside red-brown with very faint paler stripes, inside same colour, pale green at the base with wide white stripes anastomosing to a central white spot at mouth level, apex acuminate, ending in a long filamentous reddish tail to 20 cm long; spadix appendix slightly exserted from the tube, to 7 cm long by 5 mm wide, cylindrical, green, ending in a rounded, white-green, smooth or spongy apex, sessile with green bristles above the fertile part, these numerous in pistillate inflorescences only; fertile zone staminate or pistillate, subcylindrical, 2–3 by ca 0.6 cm; staminate flowers loosely arranged, 2–4-androus, anthers lilac, subsessile or on a white-green, short stalk; thecae dehiscing by an oblong pore; pistillate flowers densely arranged; ovaries bottle-shaped, to 2 mm across, pale green; stigma sessile, penicillate, white, surrounded by a black annulus. Infructescence on a nodding peduncle, cylindrical, ca 5 by 2 cm; fruits red-orange when ripe, with black stigmatic remains, ca 7 by 3 mm, up to 2 seeds per berry. Seeds globose, ca 2 mm diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Arisaema sukotaiense . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 210. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Evergreen herb to 0.7 m tall. Subterranean stem a rhizome, to 3 by 1.5 cm. Cataphylls sheathing separately petiole and peduncle, 5–7 cm long, pale red; petiole 30–45 cm long, green to pink, marbled with dark and pale stripes; leaf blade pedate with a very short rachis, ca 3 cm long; leaflets 7–9, linear-elliptic, to 30 cm long, upper side glossy green, often with a paler midvein, underside glaucous green, margins entire and undulate, base cuneate, apex long acuminate, ending in a short thread; central leaflet 13–25 by 2–4.5 cm with petiolule mottled like the petiole, this 2–3.5 cm long; lateral leaflets decreasing in size outwards to 8 by 1.5 cm, petiolulate to subsessile, the two external leaflets emerging from the same point of the rachis. Inflorescence overtopping the foliage; peduncle 40–55 by < 1 cm at the base, pink; spathe tube funnel-shaped, 5–6 by 2.5 cm near the mouth, white-green, white at the base; spathe mouth margins recurved, to 1.2 cm wide; spathe limb erect, ovate, 9–10 by 3–3.5 cm, pale green, sometimes tinged purple with a white spot at throat level, acuminate; spadix appendix long exserted from the tube, flagelliform, pendulous, conical and subulate at apex, pale green, 15–30 cm long, sessile, with a few carmine or white bristles, 2–3 mm long; fertile zone staminate or pistillate, ca 4 cm long; staminate flowers loosely arranged, 2–4-androus, anthers cream, subsessile to shortly stipitate with short, dark carmine connectives; thecae dehiscing by a round pore; pistillate flowers densely arranged; ovaries ovoid, pointed on top. Infructescence on an erect peduncle, cylindrical, to 4 by 2.5 cm; fruits red-orange when ripe, bottle-shaped, 8–10 by 4–6 mm, pointed at apex, up to 2 seeds per berry. Seeds ovoid, 6–8 by 3–5 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Arisaema wrayi . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 211. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Deciduous herb to 1 m tall. Subterranean stem a subglobose tuber, 2–4 cm across. Pseudostem to 35 by ca 1 cm, green. Leaves usually 1, sometimes 2; cataphylls to 30 cm long, green, sometimes carmine striped; petiole 10–20 cm long, green; leaf blade trifoliolate; leaflets ovate to broadly ovate, margins entire, apex acute or acuminate; central leaflet 14–25 by 7–14 cm, subsessile, or with a petiolule to 1.5 cm long, base convex; lateral leaflets smaller, slightly asymmetrical, sessile, plain green. Inflorescence held above or level with the foliage; peduncle usually longer than the petiole, 12–30 cm long, green; spathe tube subcylindrical, 3–6 by 1–3 cm, yellow-green with white stripes, white at the base; spathe mouth margins straight; spathe limb ovate-oblong, longer than the tube, horizontal, 5–8 by 2–5 cm, green, turning yellow when fading, with 5–7 wide, translucent, raised stripes, tip long acuminate; spadix appendix well exserted from the tube, 5–6 cm long, or even more, smooth, pale green, base cylindrical or slightly fusiform, 3–4 mm across, ending in a green, attenuate tail, sessile; fertile zone staminate or pistillate, 2–4 cm long, exceptionally a few staminate flowers occurring on pistillate spadices; staminate flowers loosely arranged, 2–3-androus, anthers light yellow or purple; thecae dehiscing by elongate pores; pistillate flowers densely arranged; ovaries ovoid, green; stigma on a white-green style ca 0.5 mm long, penicillate, white. Infructescence on an erect peduncle, 2.5–6 by 2–4 cm; fruits subcylindrical, apex rounded, scarlet, up to 7 seeds per berry. Seeds globose, 2–4 mm diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Arisaema yunnanense yunnanense. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 212. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Small, medium-sized or gigantic, evergreen or seasonally dormant herbs with somewhat milky latex. Stem either a hypogeal, subglobose or subcylindrical tuber, or an epigeal and slender to massive aerial, later decumbent, stem; most species stolon-producing although extent of stolon spread very variable between species. Leaves several, loosely rosulate in acaulescent plants, forming a terminal crown in arborescent species; petiole stout to very slender; petiolar sheath rather long, persistent; leaf blade peltate, ovate-cordate to sagittato– or oblong-cordate, posterior lobes rounded, shortly to almost entirely connate; basal ribs well developed; primary lateral veins pinnate, forming submarginal collective vein, 1–2 marginal veins also present, secondary and tertiary laterals arising from the primaries at a wide angle, arching strongly towards leaf margin and forming varyingly conspicuous interprimary collective veins (‘colocasioid venation’); higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescences 1–many in each floral sympodium; peduncle much shorter than to sub-equalling petiole, erect at first, declinate during fruiting in some species; spathe constricted between lower part and spathe limb, sometimes with a second constriction above staminate zone of spadix; lower part with convolute margins, usually much shorter than limb, ovoid or oblong, persistent, enlarging in fruit and then splitting open irregularly; spathe limb oblong and boat-shaped to narrowly lanceolate, erect to reflexing at anthesis, later caducous, greenish, white or deep yellow or dirty pale brown; spadix sessile to briefly stipitate, shorter than spathe; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; pistillate flower zone short, separated from staminate by narrower zone of sterile staminate flowers; sterile interstice with synandrodes, these depressed-obpyramidal, truncate, laterally compressed; interpistillar staminodes clavate; pistillate flowers an ovary ovoid or oblong, 1-locular, ovules many, hemiorthotropous, funicles relatively long, placentae 2–5, parietal, stylar region short, narrowed or not, sometimes ± absent; stigma discoid-capitate or weakly lobed; staminate flower zone cylindrical to fusiform; staminate flowers 3–6-androus, stamens connate into ± truncate synandrium overtopped by a conspicuous synconnective, thecae lateral, oblong-linear, dehiscing by apical pore; appendix erect, ± smooth, elongate-conoid to fusiform or subulate, sometimes reduced to small, mucronate stub, rarely absent. Fruitsa greenish, whitish or yellowish brown berry, obconoid or oblong, stigma remnants persistent, many-seeded, fruity-smelling at maturity. Seed ovoid to ellipsoid, testa thickish, costate, embryo axile, cylindrical, endosperm copious.</br></br>About 15 species distributed from the subtropical eastern Himalayas throughout subtropical and tropical Asia into the tropical western pacific and eastern Australia.</br></br>Four species in Thailand, none endemic. Colocasia affinis and C. fontanesii have been included in the key below (italic, non bold) since both are widespread and abundant from Assam and Bangladesh to SW China, Myanmar, and N Laos and are to be expected in N Thailand.

description: Medium to large, occasionally very large, moderate to robust, solitary to colony-forming, evergreen herb to 1 m. Stem a tuberous or elongate rhizome, 3–5(–20) cm diam., if tuberous then vertical to horizontal and variably massive, larger tubers tending to be solitary while smaller tubers tending to clusters, plants with very reduced tubers frequently with long hypogeal non tuber-bearing stolons. Leaves several together; petiole 25–80 cm sheathing for ⅓ to ⅔ length, green, occasionally purple; leaf blade oblong-ovate to suborbicular, 13–45 by 10–35 cm, hydrophobic, dull glaucous green in most clones but cultivars with the leaves variously purple flushed through to deep purple black (remaining hydrophobic), base shallowly cordate, peltate, tissue in the sinus extending 1–7 cm, apex broadly and shortly cuspidate; primary lateral veins pinnate, forming submarginal collective vein; secondary and tertiary laterals arising from the primaries at a wide angle. Inflorescences 1–3 together; peduncle 16–26 cm; spathe 13–24 cm long, constricted between the lower part and the limb; lower part ellipsoid, 3.5–5 by 1.2–1.5 cm, green; spathe limb lanceolate or lanceolate-elliptic, 10–19 by 2–5 cm, acuminate, opening slightly at the base, the rest remaining furled during anthesis, cream to golden yellow; spadix shorter than the spathe; pistillate flower zone conical 3–3.5 by 1.2 cm; ovaries globose, ca 1–3 mm diam., green; stigma subsessile, narrower than apex of ovary, barely lobed; interpistillar staminodes clavate, white, mostly exceeding the ovaries; sterile interstice slender cylindrical, 3–3.3 cm; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 4–6.5 cm by 7 mm; synandria 2–3-merous, ca 0.8 mm diam., mid-yellow; appendix narrow conical, 1.5–4.5 cm, ca ⅕–⅛ entire spadix length. Fruiting peduncle declinate; fruiting spathe ellipsoid, breaking up irregularly; fruits ca 4 mm diam., ripening yellow-brown, strongly fruity-smelling.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Colocasia esculenta . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 214. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Small to medium, slender to moderate, colony-forming, rarely solitary among rocks, evergreen herb up to 50 cm but usually much less. Stem a globose tuber, 1–1.5 cm diam., with numerous stolons to 45 cm long, ca 3 mm diam. Leaves few together; petiole 12–27 cm, sheathing for almost ½ length, pale green to sheaths reddish brown; leaf blade narrowly oblong-ovate cordate, peltate, 8–25 by 3.5–15 cm, adaxially pale to mid-green, sometimes with darker green or more rarely purple areas between the primary lateral veins, slightly glaucous abaxially; primary lateral veins well demarcated; interprimary veins forming a weak interprimary collecting vein. Inflorescences 1–3 together; peduncle slender, 6.5–20 cm; spathe 6.5–16 cm; lower spathe ellipsoid-globose, 1.5–4 by ca 1.3 cm, medium-green; spathe limb narrowly lanceolate, 5–12 by 1–3.5 cm, finely acuminate, dirty yellow to pale orange-yellow, spreading fully and then reflexing at anthesis; spadix shorter than to equalling the spathe, 5–9 cm long; pistillate flower zone 1.2–1.4 by 0.5 cm, with 4–6 rows of whitish weakly nail- to peg-like staminodes at base; ovaries subglobose, ca 1.1 mm diam., green, sometimes speckled white, not interspersed with staminodes; stigma 3-lobed; sterile interstice tapering, 1.7–2.5 cm long, lower part with weakly clavate staminodes, upper part with rhobohexagonal synandrodes, the whole interstice ivory; staminate flower zone1.1–1.4 cm by ca 4 mm; synandria ca 1 mm diam., white to pale orange; appendix 2.5–3.5 cm by 1–3 mm (½–⅓ of spadix length), tapering cylindrical, usually sessile onto the staminate zone, sometimes briefly but distinctly stipitate, acute, rough, creamy yellow to purple, usually with several rows of staminodes at base. Fruiting peduncle reflexed, fruiting spathe ovoid, ca 2.5 by 1 cm; fruits not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Colocasia fallax . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 215. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Massive, pachycaul, evergreen herb to 3.5 m with copious milky latex. Stem erect to decumbent. Leaves several together; petiole waxy-white glaucous, to 1.5 m long, lower ½ of the length sheathing; leaf blade ovate-cordate, peltate, 25–160 by 17–120 cm, base deeply cordate, apex short acuminate, pale green adaxially, strikingly waxy-white glaucous (pruinose) abaxially; primary lateral veins pronounced below, impressed above; interprimary veins forming well-defined interprimary collecting veins. Inflorescences 5–10 in a distichous arrangement the axiof a foliage leaf; peduncle cylindrical, 30–80 by 1–2 cm, each one with a membranous cataphyll, nearly equalling the length of peduncle; spathe 11–25 cm; lower spathe ellipsoid, 3–6 by 1.5–2 cm, glaucous green; spathe limb boat-shaped, 8–19 by 2–3 cm, erect, white; spadix 9–20 cm; pistillate flower zone conical, 3–4 by 1–1.75 cm; ovaries oblong-ovoid, ca 2.5 by 1.5 mm, green; stigma capitate, white; sterile interstice markedly constricted, 3–4.5 cm long; staminate flower zone slightly fusiform, 5–14 cm long; synandria ca 2.5 by 2.5 mm, waxy white, synconnective slightly convex; appendix conical, acute, 1–5 mm long. Fruiting peduncle erect; fruiting spathe ellipsoid, ca 10 by 3 cm; fruits globose, ca 3 mm diam., ripening pale yellow, smelling of over ripe pineapple.

description: Medium to large, robust, terrestrial, perennial herbs to 1 m. Stems rhizomatous, 20–40 by 3–7 cm, producing stolons; stolons 6–10 per plant, 15–20 cm long, 4 mm diam., trailing horizontally, pale green; without tubercles. Leaves 5–6 together; petiole cylindrical, 50 × 1 cm, pale greenish, pubescent; leaf blade ovate-cordate, peltate, ca 40 by 25 cm, membranaceous, adaxially glossy medium green, abaxially pale green, pilose; primary lateral veins pinnate, 7–9 pairs per side; interprimary veins forming moderately well-defined interprimary collecting veins. Inflorescences 2–4 together; peduncle cylindrical, 20 cm long, shorter than petiole, pale green, pubescent; spathe constricted between lower tubular part and limb; lower part fusiform, 3–6 by 1.2 cm, greenish; spathe limb oblong-lanceolate, 13–18 by 4–6 cm, lower part open, upper part convolute at anthesis, erect, not reflexed, yellowish; spadix sessile, ca 9.5 cm long, shorter than spathe; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, 2 by 1 cm; ovaries ovoid to oblong, 1.5 mm long, green; stylar region short; stigma discoid-capitate, slightly paler; sterile interstice tapering cylindrical, narrower than either fertile zone, ca 3.5 cm long, covered with synandrodes, white; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 3.5 by 0.7 cm; synandria 8–11-merous, ca 2 mm diam., yellowish; appendix elongate conical, 3.5 by 0.5 cm, rugose at base, pale purplish yellow, paler basally. Fruit not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description:
Small to medium, evergreen or less often seasonally dormant herbs with procumbent to erect rhizomes and short to long stolons; plants that grow slowly have short, rugged rhizomes, while quick-growing plants have more slender rhizomes with 0.5–1(–2) cm long internodes. Cataphylls often present in flowering plants, in some species also in non-flowering plants, sub-2-keeled; petiole elongate, basally sheathing; leaf blade elliptic-ovate to strap-shaped, vernationconvolute, base attenuate-truncate to cordate. Inflorescence usually shortly pedunculate; spathe with a basal tube, (the kettle), with united margins, an upper tube (sometimes twisted) with fused margins, and a terminal limb which opens into a flat, ovate surface, or may be more or less spirally coiled; a distinctive “collar” or “collar zone” is often found at the transition between the upper tube and the spathe limb; the inside kettle wall sometimes with depressions (alveoli), in the upper part; spadix small, included in the kettle with a basal pistillate part, a part with olfactory bodies, a thin, naked interstice, a staminate part, and a small naked appendix that at the first day of anthesis is adnate to the base of the flap at the top of the kettle; pistillate flowers 4–8, naked, upright, in a single connate whorl; styles outwards-curved; stigma ovate-elliptic to emarginate, occasionally trilobed; ovules 3–20 per pistil, erect, on the adaxial wall; staminate flowers 25–80(–130); thecae 2 per stamen, with a small horn, through which pollen is extruded. Infructescence a sub-ovoid to globular syncarp-like, multiple fruit, each part ultimately splitting at the adaxial side and becoming star-shaped, follicle-like, a few species splitting in a septicidal/septifragal-ceratium manner. Infructescence at maturity raised above the ground by a quickly-extending peduncle. Seeds ellipsoid, rough, mostly with endosperm (but see C. ciliata).</br></br>About 60 aquatic to amphibious species in Asia from India to New Guinea. Eight species have been included for Thailand. None endemic.</br></br>E c o l o g y.— In and along streams and rivers, in fresh and brackish tidal zones, sometimes also in forest pools, in lowland rainforests, often forming large submerged or emergent stands. The rhizomes and stolons are usually deeply buried, sometimes only with the spathe limb and the upper part of the spathe protruding above the ground. In more quickly running water the plants are mostly rooted in sand or between stones and rocks while, in more slowly running water, they are found deep in mud.</br></br>Species of Cryptocoryne fall into a number of natural groups, correlated with morphology, distribution and chromosome numbers (e.g., Arends et al. op.cit.). The chromosome numbers form dysploid (“aneuploid”) as well as euploid series, where the different numbers are characteristic of the species/groups in question (see under each species). A number of tri-, penta- and hexaploids are known, of which most reproduce only vegetatively.</br></br>In some species, plants growing in deeper water tend to have larger leaves, a longer spathe tube and a longer peduncle than those growing in shallow water or as emergents.</br></br>Several exotic species are cultivated in nurseries in Thailand for use as aquarium plants. Their identity may be checked in: Jacobsen, N., 1987. Cryptocoryne in Dassanayake, M.D. and F.R. Fosberg eds. A Revised Handbook to the Flora of Ceylon, Vol. VI: 85–99, and species 
occurring in neighbouring Peninsular Malaysia may be consulted in Othman, Jacobsen, & Mashhor. 2009.Cryptocoryne of Peninsular Malaysia 1–102, Penerbit Universiti Sains Malaysia.

description: Rhizome short and rugged, sometimes slender with long internodes. Runners long, slender. Leaves green to brownish purple, upper surface purplish green to green, lower surface red to greenish with reddish veins; leaf blade narrowly ovate, with a truncate to narrowly cordate base, 5–15 by 1–4 cm, surface between the veins smooth to bullate (largest specimens in deep, not quite so fast-running water, small compact specimens in faster-running water; emerged specimens with greenish, crumpled leaves); petiole 5–15 cm long; spathe 10–22 cm long; peduncle 1–3 cm long; kettle 1–2 cm long, white, inside purplish in the upper half; tube 2–12 cm long, white, the upper part dark purplish on the outside; limb 3–7 cm long, spirally twisted, black purple, upper part sometimes greenish, somewhat rough; collar elongate, present but more or less concealed in the spirally twisted limb; pistillate flowers 5–8, purplish to purple or greenish and purple spotted, more or less papillose; stigmas ovate to emarginate; olfactory bodies irregularly rounded, upper surface more or less rough, yellow to purplish spotted; staminate flowers 40–60, smooth. Infructescence ovoid. Seeds brownish, surface somewhat rough; endosperm present, embryo cone-shaped, with an undifferentiated plumula. Chromosome number: 2n = 34.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Rhizome to 1 cm thick. Stolons often with a metallic, blue-grey colour. Leaves green to brownish marbled, smooth (sometimes slightly undulate towards the margins); leaf blade lanceolate, 10–30 by 1–2 cm, with lateral veins, margin entire; spathe 10–20 cm long; kettle 0.8–1.5 cm long, more or less reddish inside and with alveoli in the upper part; tube 5–15 cm long, slightly twisted; limb short, 1–2.5 (–4) cm long, sometimes more or less upright and spirally twisted at anthesis, later becoming recurved, greyish to cream, with reddish to brown irregular to circular or elongate markings which may sometimes cover the surface completely, the markings may also be missing; collar absent; pistillate flowers 4–7; stigma more or less vertical, ovate; olfactory bodies more or less rounded, often depressed in the centre, yellowish to greenish; staminate flowers 80–120. Infructescence white to greenish to purplish, elongate globular, 1–1.5 cm long, surface smooth. Seeds brownish, rugose, 5–8 mm long; endosperm present, embryo cone-shaped with an undifferentiated plumula. Chromosome number: 2n = 36.

description: Like var. ciliata except that the leaf blade is broader (10–30 by 4–10 cm) and, instead of the stolons being long, they are 3–15 cm long, erect, non-rooting, branching at the internodes, and quite fragile, breaking off at the nodes and rooting later; flowers sterile, fruits not developing. Chromosome number: 2n = 33 (triploid).</br></br>N o t e s.— The triploids are sterile and their only mode of reproduction is by their fragile runners. Plants with 2n = 33 can be regarded as a triploid cytotype and can be accepted at the variety level.</br></br>The exact distribution of diploids and triploids is not known; only that triploids have been found in Bangkok, Peninsular Malaysia (Johor), Singapore, Sumatra (Bintan), and Sarawak.

description: Leaves smooth to somewhat bullate, upper surface green to dark green with markings to purplish or purple, lower surface paler with reddish veins or shades to dark red; leaf blade narrowly cordate to cordate, 5–15 by 2–10 cm; petiole 10–40 cm long, longest in continuously submerged specimens from slow-running water; spathe 20–35(–50) cm long, white on the outside, sometimes brownish/greenish towards the apex; kettle white inside, 1–3 cm long; tube 15–40 cm long, white inside; limb more or less flat, 3–5 cm long, more or less backwards twisted, ovate with a shorter or longer point, surface more or less smooth, yellow; collar broad, yellow, gradually merging into the white tube; pistillate flowers 5–8 whitish; stigmas rounded, ovate, more or less upright; staminate flowers 40–60(–80). Infructescence more or less purplish, ovoid, broad and shortly pointed, 1.5–2 cm long, surface smooth to rough. Seeds brownish, rugose, ca 10 mm long; endosperm present, embryo conical with an undifferentiated plumula. Chromosome number: 2n = 34.

description: Leaves smooth to somewhat bullate, upper surface dark green with markings to purplish or purple, lower with reddish veins or shades to dark red; leaf blade narrowly ovate (sometimes with a cordate base), 5–16 by 3–7 cm; petiole 5–30 cm long, longest in continuously submerged specimens from slow-running water; spathe 7–20 cm long, white on the outside, brownish/greenish towards the apex; kettle white inside, sometimes reddish in the lower half, 1.5–3 cm long; tube 4–15 cm long, white inside; limb more or less flat, 2–4 cm long, more or less backwards twisted, ovate with a shorter or longer point, surface more or less smooth, yellow to red-brownish shaded, if shaded, then more intensively so towards the margins and the apex; collar broad, yellow, gradually merging into the white tube; spadix with 5–8 whitish pistillate flowers; stigmas ovate to emarginate, occasionally three-partite, more or less upright; staminate flowers 30–60. Infructescence unknown. Chromosome number: 2n = 102.

description: Leaves 15–70 by 1–4 cm, usually submerged, rather flaccid, green to brownish, slightly to strongly bullate, midrib conspicuous, lateral veins less so; emergent leaves are shorter and often not as bullate as the submerged ones; spathe with a long tube, 10–30(–40) cm long; limb with a rather long and rather open to somewhat tight spiral, colour markings on the limb surface usually greyish or yellowish, mostly with shorter or longer purplish markings of varying intensities. Chromosome number: 2n = 36.

description: Leaves narrowly linear to lanceolate, green to brownish (with markings in some exposed habitats), smooth to undulate at the margin, 10–30 by 0.2–1.5(–2.5) cm; margin entire to finely or irregularly denticulate, upright to flat on the soil, rather stiff (in shaded habitats more lax), in some forms the leaves almost disappear during the monsoon period and become small, 2–4 cm long and terete; spathe 10–20 cm long; kettle 1–2.5 cm long, more or less reddish inside and with alveoli in the upper part; tube 2–10 cm long, slightly to somewhat twisted; limb 2–8 cm long, more or less spirally twisted, yellowish to greyish to greenish, with short to long, usually purple (sometimes black purple) markings (before anthesis occasionally reddish), these sometimes covering the surface almost completely, or missing, or the limb almost white-grounded with a few faint markings, or entirely white. Chromosome number: 2n = 36, 54.

description: Rhizome to 1 cm thick. Stolons with exceptionally large scale leaves (> 1 cm). Leaves strap-shaped, to 30 by 0.5–1 cm, smooth to somewhat undulating at the margin (sometimes also finely denticulate), green to brownish marbled, apex rather abruptly acute; leaves disappearing during the rainy period or becoming small, 2–4 cm long and terete; spathe 8–12 cm long; kettle 2–2.5 cm long, with a constriction just below the staminate flowers, whitish in the lower part, purplish in the upper part which also has alveoli in the wall; tube 4–5 cm long, greyish on the outside; limb to 3.5 cm long, (upright to) somewhat bent backwards, with irregular purplish, rounded protuberances that are sometimes more or less transversely orientated, base surface colour dark yellowish, throat spotted; collar absent; pistillate flowers 5–6 with vertical, elliptic stigmas; olfactory bodies cream-coloured, finely spotted, irregularly lobed to almost toothed; staminate flowers 80–120. Infructescence ovoid. Chromosome number: 2n = 36.

description: Creeping rhizome with strongly developed contractile roots. Leaves linear to lanceolate with a pronounced main vein, to 30 by 2 cm, gradually tapering to a fine point, base narrowly to shortly attenuate, margin somewhat undulate, irregularly denticulate, green and, under exposed light conditions, brownish tinged and with darker markings; petiole to 8 cm long, reddish in sunlight; spathe ca 5–6 cm long; kettle ca 1.5 by 0.6 cm, with a thickened wall just about the middle inside, lower inside wall white, upper part with alveoli; valve whitish, red streaked, walls red to reddish with small white blotches continuing upwards to the tube; tube ca 2–3 cm in length; limb shortly upright to obliquely forward twisted, the inner surface evenly rough throughout, evenly brown to red purple; collar absent; pistillate flowers 6; stigmas round, almost vertical; olfactory bodies irregularly rounded, purplish; staminate flowers about 50–60, yellow, surface of the thecae rough from protruding cells. Infructescence unknown. Chromosome number: 2n = 36.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Rhizome creeping with distinctly thickened yearly growths. Leaves linear, to 40 by 1.5 cm, gradually tapering to a fine point, base narrowly attenuate, margin somewhat undulate, smooth to irregularly denticulate, green and, under exposed light conditions, with a brownish tinge and with brownish markings; spathe ca 5–7 cm long; kettle ca 1–2 by 0.5–1 cm, with a thickened wall inside just about the middle, lower inside wall white, upper part with alveoli, red to reddish with small white blotches continuing upwards through the tube which is ca 1–2 cm in length, a 1–3 times spirally twisted limb (before anthesis), with purple, irregular, very pronounced transverse ridges on the surface (most pronounced on the lower part), and a pronounced purple collar structure; pistillate flowers ca 6; stigma round, almost vertical; olfactory bodies distinctly irregular (rounded) with protruding cells, purplish; staminate flowers about 80–120, yellow, surface of the thecae rough from protruding cells. Infructescence splitting in a septicidal/septifragal-ceratium-like manner, greenish to purplish, globose to ovate, 1–1.5 cm long, smooth. Seeds brownish, 5–8 mm, rugose; endosperm present; embryo conical with an undifferentiated plumula. Chromosome number: 2n = 36.

description: Moderate to very large, slender to very robust, secondary hemiepiphytic, evergreen lianes with abundant trichosclereids. Stem root-climbing or less often prostrate, usually producing long flagelliform shoots with reduced cataphylls and abundant clasping roots. Leaves several to many, distichous to spiro-distichous and often forming conspicuous tufts at the tips of active shoots; petiole long-channelled, pulvinate apically and basally; petiolar sheath long, marcescent to deciduous, sometimes decomposing to conspicuous net-fibrous mass; leaf blade lanceolate, elliptic, elliptic-oblong, entire, pinnatipartite or pinnatisect, rarely minutely perforate (E. pinnatum), often oblique; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into marginal vein, secondary and often tertiary venation parallel-pinnate, higher order venation and sometimes tertiary venation reticulate. Inflorescences 1(–5) in each floral sympodium; peduncle relatively short, sometimes obscured by a mass of netted fibrous degraded cataphylls; spathe boat-shaped, withering after anthesis, usually deciduous; spadix subcylindrical, conical, sessile or stipitate, shorter than spathe; flowers bisexual, the lowermost ones pistillate or sterile, perigone absent; gynoecium with ovary subtetragonal-prismatic- cylindrical, truncate, 1-loculate; ovules usually 2, more rarely 4 or 6–8, anatropous, funicle short, placenta parietal or near base of parietal partial septa; stylar region prismatic as broad or broader than ovary; stigma umbonate to oblong-linear and longitudinal. Infructescence comprised of a 1–8-seeded monsterocarp with stylar region deciduous at maturity, mostly ripening dull orange. Seed reniform, testa thickish, brittle, smooth, embryo curved, endosperm copious.</br></br>Approximately 15 species from Japan (Ryukyu Islands) to Australia (Queensland) and India (Manipur) to Oceania (Cook Islands: Rarotonga). Three species in Thailand, none endemic, one (E. auruem) adventive or seminaturalized as an escape from cultivation.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Epipremnum  . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 232. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Very large root-climbing secondary hemiepiphyte to 16 m. Stem (adult) 5–40 mm diam., with prominent irregular whitish longitudinal crests, active portions of stem mid-green to pale yellow-green, sometimes with large obscure dull yellow to white variegations, depending on leaf variegation, older stems with distinctive matte to sub-lustrous orange-brown papery epidermis; flagellate foraging shoots common, arising high in the canopy and reaching the ground. Leaves scattered on lower stem, becoming clustered distally; petiole 19.5–50 cm by 3–15 mm, canaliculate, smooth, mid-green to rather bright yellow-green, apical and basal pulvini barely greater in diameter than petiole; petiolar sheath extending to mid-way along apical geniculum, at first submembranaceous, soon drying chartaceous and degrading to untidy, slightly netted weak fibres, then falling to leave a smooth, mid-brown scar; leaf blade 10–93 by 5–60 cm, entire (juvenile) to irregularly pinnatifid, ovate to elliptic in outline, sub-coriaceous, apex acute to acuminate, base moderately cordate, divisions pinnatifid to pinnatipartite; pinnae up to half the length of the lamina wide, apex truncate, dull to somewhat glossy mid-green, usually irregularly yellow or white variegated, rarely entirely mid-green; pinnae each with 1 (very rarely more except for the terminal pinna) compound primary lateral vein and several to rather many interprimary veins, individual elements of the compound vein diverging at ca 10° from various points along the pinna; interprimary and secondary venation mostly remaining sub-parallel to compound primary vein; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescences almost never produced.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Epipremnum aureum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 233. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Large to gigantic root-climber, to 30 m. Stem 10–35 mm diam., glossy dark green, smooth, older stems mid-brown. Leaves evenly distributed but lower ones often falling and then leaves tending to become clustered towards stem apices; petiole 33–62.5 cm by 6–20 mm, canaliculate, dark green to slightly glaucous, smooth; apical pulvinus 20–25 by 5–12 mm, basal pulvinus 2–4 cm by 7–15 mm; petiolar sheath extending to half way along petiole, at first sub-membranaceous, soon drying scarious, later breaking into regular sections and falling to leave a somewhat roughened, mid-brown scar; leaf blade entire, oblong-elliptic, 5.5–100 by 8.5–48 cm, slightly falcate, coriaceous, glossy bright green, margins hyaline and becoming prominently reddish in exposed situations, apex acute to slightly acuminate, base unequal-rounded, one side often produced into a rounded to truncate posterior lobe; primary lateral veins parallel, barely or not differentiated from interprimary veins; interprimary veins very numerous, prominent, remaining parallel to primary vein. Inflorescence solitary, rarely two or more together; peduncle 5–8 cm by 4–10 mm. Spathe canoe-shaped, 16–33.5 by 5.5–14 cm when pressed flat, shortly but stoutly tapering, gaping at anthesis and then falling before anthesis is complete, exterior green, interior waxy-glaucous to dull yellow, smelling strongly of peanut butter; spadix 15.5–28.5 by 1.5–4.5 cm, sessile, cylindrical, bluntly tapering towards the apex, orange at anthesis; flowers 2.5–4 mm diam. across the style; ovary 3–10 by 2.5–4 mm, cylindrical-ellipsoid, basal part strongly compressed; stylar region 4–10 by 1.5–4 mm, acroscopic-trapezoid, robust, apex flattened; stigma 0.8–3 by 0.1–0.5 mm, linear. Infructescences ripening deep yellow, stylar region greatly enlarged.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Epipremnum giganteum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 234. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Large root-climbing robust secondary hemiepiphytes to 15 m. Stem 5–40 mm diam., lustrous green with prominent irregular greyish crests, older stems with distinctive matte to sub-lustrous pale brown papery epidermis. Leaves scattered on lower stem, becoming somewhat clustered towards stem apices; petiole 19.5–60 cm by 3–13 mm, canaliculate, dark green, smooth; apical pulvinus 16–70 by 0.3–0.5 cm, basal pulvinus 3–7 by 1–1.5 cm; petiolar sheath extending ⅓–¾ along petiole, rarely (poorly developed leaves) reaching apical pulvinus, at first membranaceous, soon drying chartaceous and disintegrating into untidy partially netted fibres, later falling to leave a smooth, mid-brown scar; leaf blade 10–93 by 5–60 cm, entire (juvenile plants) to regularly pinnate, ovate to elliptic in outline, sub-membranaceous, lustrous dark green, rarely slightly to intensely blue-green and glaucous above, apex acute to acuminate, base rounded to slightly cordate, divisions pinnatifid to pinnatisect, occasionally midrib ± naked at sinus; pinnae 1.2–6.5 cm wide, apex truncate to acute, terminal pinna shallowly sinuous, many individuals with minute to somewhat well developed pellucid dots especially adjacent to the midrib, pellucid dots often perforating and enlarging, sometimes extending to blade margin (then fenestrations often additional to fully developed pinnae); primary lateral veins 1 per pinna; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, rarely two or more together, at anthesis partially to almost completely obscured by netted fibres; peduncle 5.5–21.5 cm by 4–10 mm; spathe canoe-shaped, 7–23.5 by 3–15 cm when pressed flat, stoutly attenuate to 15 mm, gaping at anthesis and then falling before anthesis is complete, exterior green, later dull greenish yellow to mid-green, interior dull yellow (reported as white by some collectors) at anthesis; spadix 8.5–25 by 1.1–3.5 cm, sessile, cylindrical, bluntly tapering towards the apex, glaucous grey-green to greenish cream, dark yellow or greenish white at anthesis; flowers 3–7 mm diam., across the style; ovary 4–12 by 2–7 mm, cylindrical-ellipsoid, basal part slightly compressed; stylar region 3–7 by 1.5 4 mm, acroscopic-trapezoid, rather robust, apex flattened; stigma 2–6 by 0.1–0.5 mm, linear. Infructescence mid-green, rarely somewhat to prominently glaucous, stylar region greatly enlarged, transversely dehsicent, the abscission developing at the base of the massive stylar region and this falling to expose the ovary cavity full of orange pulp.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Small, slender, seasonally dormant, rarely evergreen, weakly laticiferous herbs to 35 cm tall. Stems tuberous and/or stoloniferous, tubers small, depressed-globose to somewhat irregular, stolons comparatively robust. Leaves 1-few together; petiole terete, slender; petiolar sheath very short, its protective role taken over by the subtending prophyll or cataphyll; leaf blade cordate-sagittate, sagittate or hastate, mid-green, sometimes paler green or silver-grey variegated; primary lateral veins pinnate or mostly arising at petiole insertion, forming an arching submarginal collective vein, 1–2 marginal veins also present; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence 1–2 in each floral sympodium, with sympodia often enriching and thus several inflorescences together, appearing with leaf in seasonally dormant species or with new shoot activity in evergreen species; peduncle subequal or longer than petiole, slender; spathe slender, not distinctly constricted; lower spathe very slender, persistent, tightly convolute around pistillate flowers; spathe limb oblong-lanceolate, erect to reflexed and ± revolute at anthesis, briefly marcescent; spadix subequal or longer than spathe, slender; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; pistillate flower zone adnate to spathe, 2–7-flowered, ± biseriate, separated from staminate flower zone by short sterile zone; pistillate flowers with gynoecium oblong to lageniform, 1-locular, ovule 1, placenta parietal to subbasal (morphologically basal); stylar region very short; stigma subcapitate; staminate flower zone subulate to cylindrical, fertile to apex (not in Thailand) or with free or fused synandria at the apex, or with a long, terminal appendix (the last not in Thailand); staminate flower a 3-androus peltate synandrium, truncate, hexagonal, elongated in sense of spadix axis, shallow, stipitate, connective strongly dilated; thecae short, subglobose, remote, almost pendent from margin, dehiscing by pores. Synandria lower ones very few, ± remote, apiculiform, upper ones few, consisting of tiny, peltate synandrodes. Fruit an ellipsoid to globose berry, style persistent, pericarp thin, 1-seeded, white. Seed ellipsoid, testa smooth, very thin, embryo large, ellipsoid, light green, endosperm absent</br></br>Eight species distributed from Myanmar to SW China (Yunnan), south to N Borneo (Sarawak, Brunei). Four species in Thailand, one (H. kerrii) endemic. All Thai species are frequently (but not obligately) associated with limestone.</br></br>The cordate leaves are superficially similar to those of several Typhonium species, with which Hapaline shares reticulate venation, but differs by being laticiferous and by the synandriate staminate flowers, and an appendix (where present) clothed with synandrodia. The pistillate flower zone in Typhonium is hemispherical to conical-cylindrical while that of Hapaline comprises a single longitudinal row of pistillate flowers on a spadix axis adnate to the lower spathe.

description: Slender, tuberous, deciduous herb to 30 cm high. Tuber globose to compressed globose, 5–12 by 4–7 mm, producing rhizomes 2–6.5 cm by 2–3 mm, sparsely to densely clothed with numerous papery cataphylls. Leaves solitary or up to 5 together; petiole 4–30 cm by 0.5–3 mm; leaf blade variably sagittate, occasionally slightly constricted at the junction of the anterior and posterior lobes, 5.5–17 by 1.5–8.5 cm, margins smooth to slightly crispulate, apex attenuate-acuminate to attenuate, posterior lobes subacute to slightly rounded, divergent, medium to dark green, often irregularly blotched pale green or greyish. Inflorescences 1–3 together; peduncle 9–17 cm by 0.5–1 mm; spathe 4–8.7 cm long; lower spathe clasping, 1.5–3.3 cm by 2 mm; spathe limb elliptic, 2.5–6.5 cm by 4–11 mm, apex acute, minutely apiculate, base long-decurrent into lower spathe; spadix 3–6 cm by 1.5–1.75 mm, free portion 2.8 –5.5 cm, cylindrical, tapering apically into an appendix composed of free synandrodes; ovary ovoid, 2 by 1.2 mm, ca 7 in two staggered rows; style ca 0.5 mm long; stigma capitate, ca 0.33 mm diam.; synandria elongate-elliptic in plan view, 5–11 by 1–1.5 mm. description: Small, tuberous, deciduous, occasionally evergreen, perennial herb to 32 cm tall. Tuber globose, 7–17 by 7–13 mm, never producing rhizomes. Leaves several together; petiole slender 8–19 cm by 0.5–1.5 mm, each subtended by a membranous, soon drying papery cataphyll; petiolar sheath very short; leaf blade cordate-elliptic, 5.5–16 by 2.7–10.5 cm, thinly coriaceous, dark to mid-green, occasionally with pale green median blotches, margins smooth, apex acuminate, posterior lobes rounded, ± parallel to slightly overlapping. description: Rather robust, deciduous perennial herb to 32 cm tall. Tuber cylindrical, 3 by 1 cm, rhizomatous in appearance. Leaves few together; petiole 25–27.5 cm by 2– 3 mm; leaf blade hastate, junction of anterior lobe with posterior lobes strongly constricted, 13.3–23.5 by 5.5–9.4 cm, thin-textured, dark green, heavily marked with diffuse pale green and silver-grey patches, margins smooth, apex acuminate to subacuminate, posterior lobes acute to subacuminate, strongly divergent. description: Slender, tuberous, deciduous perennial herb to 30 cm tall. Tuber compressed globose with numerous conspicuous stolons, tuber 2–2.4 by 1–1.5 cm, stolons to 15 cm long. Leaves few together; petiole 9–20 cm by ca 2 mm; leaf blade elliptic-cordiform, 5.2–15.5 by 2.9–8.5 cm, thin-textured, mid-green, margins smooth, apex acute to slightly attenuate, posterior lobes overlapping. Inflorescences 1–4 together, emerging before the leaves, occasionally with them; peduncle 18–24 cm by 1–2 mm; spathe 5–8.5 cm long; lower spathe clasping, 1–1.5 cm by 1–1.5 mm; spathe limb oblong-elliptic, 3–6.5 by 1–1.1 cm, apex acute, base decurrent into lower spathe; spadix 4.5–9 cm by 1–2 mm, free portion cylindrical, 3.5–5 cm, tapering apically into a short appendix composed of free synandrodes; ovary 1–3, compressed ellipsoid to bottle-shaped, 2 by 1 mm; style ca 0.5 mm long; stigma capitate, ca 0.33 mm diam.; synandria 3–4 by 1 mm, oblong in plan view. description: Minute to very large, solitary to clustering, erect to decumbent, less often creeping, usually strongly aromatic, evergreen mesophytes, rarely rheophytes, very rarely helophytes. Leaves mostly spirally arranged, sometimes with conspicuous reddish extrafloral nectaries; petioles terete to D-shaped in cross-section, lower part sheathing, almost always with a pulvinus mid-way along, rarely terminal at the leaf blade insertion; petiolar sheath persistent to marcescent; leaf blade simple, cordate to oblanceolate, glabrous; venation striate. Inflorescences several together; spathe persistent until maturation of fruit, boat-shaped or constricted into a lower convolute portion and distally a variously opening spathe limb, exterior smooth or externally ribbed and keeled along the dorsal midline, apex apiculate to strongly mucronate; spadix with pistillate and staminate flower zones occasionally separated by a naked to staminode-bearing interstice, and staminate part often secreting reddish to brown resin prior to or during anthesis; pistillate flowers each associated with a single staminode, rarely not (not in Thailand); ovary with style extremely short; stigma button-like to discoid, sometimes weakly lobed; staminate flowers 2–4androus; filaments very short; anthers opening by short apical longitudinal slits concealed, or not, by an expanded connective forming a flat cap. Infructescences pendent during development and at maturity, fruits contained within the persistent and often enlarged lower spathe; fruiting spathe dehiscent from the base upwards, usually the spathe circumscissile at the insertion of the peduncle then splitting into a few irregular strips and these curling upwards to reveal the ripe fruit; fruit a many-seeded, small, translucent, greenish berry, smelling of overripe fruit or butyric acid.</br></br>Homalomena is one of the most abundant, speciose and least well understood mesophytic aroid genera in tropical Asia. Furthermore, it is now becoming the focus of interest for pharmaceutical research into the terpenoids and flavonoids occurring in all tissues; such studies require a sound basis of taxonomic understanding.</br></br>The lack of a reliable taxonomy is owing to many factors, not least the poor state of preservation of many of the historical types coupled with the cryptic nature of most of the systematically significant characters, notably the presence, absence and disposition of sterile flowers and the generally large and complex vegetative structures that do not lend themselves readily to traditional herbarium vouchering methods. Another factor is the brief anthesis period which means that even well-prepared herbarium specimens are frequently useless to taxonomists because many significant structures on the inflorescences deliquesce soon after flowering or are damaged by the most frequent inflorescence visitors, chrysomelid beetles, before preservation.</br></br>At least 250 species, well over half yet to be described, occurring from Indo-Malaya to SW China eastwards through tropical Australasia as far as western Oceania (Solomon Islands) with major centres of diversity in Sumatra, Borneo and New Guinea.</br></br>Seven species in Thailand with an eighth, new species known (and included in the key) from material not suitable for formal description. This total is decidedly provisional as the genus is very poorly collected. It is conceivable that the true number of indigenous species is a dozen or more. Several exotic species are cultivated as ornamentals in the Kingdom, including neotropical H. wallisii and H. crinipes.

description: Moderate, somewhat robust, stemless to decumbent-stemmed herb to 60 cm, smelling of camphor. Leaves several together; petioles to 35 cm long, pale to mid-green with slightly darker longitudinal 1–2 cm by 0.5 mm streaks; petiolar sheath 4–7 cm, margins membranous, persistent; leaf blade ovate-sagittate to elliptic-sagitatte or lanceolate-sagittate, 20–30 by 10–17 cm, base cordato-sagittate, sinus wide (ca 5 cm) apex acute to long-acuminate, with a ca 2 mm tubular mucro, thinly coriaceous, mid-green; posterior costae each with 4–6 primary lateral veins arising more or less together; anterior costa with 4–6 primary lateral veins and a similar number of virtually indistinguishable interprimary veins diverging from the midrib at 45°; secondary venation striate. Inflorescences 1–2 together; peduncle 10–18 cm, erect (developing and floral) to declinate (after anthesis and fruiting), coloured as for petioles; spathe oblong, 8–10 cm long, gaping at anthesis, then closing again, pale green; spadix tapering-cylindrical, 7–9 cm, sub-equalling spathe, stipitate; stipe ca 5 mm long; pistillate flower zone 1.5–3 by 1 cm; ovaries ovoid-globose, ca 2 mm diam., with an associated clavate staminode ca equalling height of the ovary; stigma sessile, capitate, ovary pale green; staminode ivory; staminate flower zone 5.5–6 cm by 5 mm; staminate flowers rhombohexagonal in plan view, ca 1–2 mm diam., each comprising two stamens overtopped by a large connective, white. Infructescence when ripe shedding spathe by slightly ragged basal abscission; fruits dull orange yellow, smelling of overripe fruit.

description: Small, clump-forming, evergreen, weakly aromatic herb to 35 cm but usually much less. Stem erect, older plants creeping, 1–1.5 cm thick. Leaves few to many together; petioles 10–13 cm, green or pinkish-tinged; petiolar sheath 3–4 cm, margins membranous; leaf blade vary variable, oblong-lanceolate to ovate-elliptic or broadly to narrowly trapezoid, 6–12.5 by 3.5–5 cm, base deltoid, truncate to very slightly cordate, apex acuminate, with a 1–2 mm tubular mucro, thinly coriaceous; primary lateral veins 4–7, robust; interprimary veins much finer, striate; secondary venation almost invisible. Inflorescences 1–3 together; peduncle 3–5.5 cm, green to cherry red; spathe ovoid-lanceolate, 2–2.5 by ca 0.75 cm, apex rostrate, ca 2.5 mm long, gaping at anthesis and then soon closing, medium-green to pinkish or cherry red; spadix tapering-cylindrical, 2–2.5 by ca 0.5 cm, equalling spathe, stipitate; stipe ca 3.5 mm long; pistillate flower zone ca 15 by 3 mm; ovary ovoid or globose, ca 1.5 mm diam., with an associated clavate staminode ca ½ height of the ovary; style short; stigma capitate; ovary pale green, staminode white; staminate flower zone ca 1 cm by 3 mm; staminate flowers each with two stamens, white, ca 0.5 mm diam. description: Very small to small, clump-forming evergreen, very slightly aromatic, lithophytic (in Thailand obligately so, elsewhere not) herb to 25 cm but usually very much smaller. Stem erect, older plants creeping, 0.5–1 cm thick. Leaves many together; petioles 5–11(–15) cm, green or pinkish-tinged or deep purple, refractive; petiolar sheath 1–4 cm, margins membranous; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate to ovate-elliptic or ovate-lanceolate, 6–12 cm by 3.5–5 cm, base rounded to very slightly cordate, apex rounded, minutely apiculate, with a 1–2 mm tubular mucro, softly coriaceous and frequently with a velvety appearance owing to refractive cells (not pubescence), green or pinkish-tinged or deep purple; primary lateral veins 4–6 diverging; interprimary veins much finer, striate; secondary venation almost invisible. Inflorescences 1–6 together; peduncle 2–5(–7) cm, green or pinkish-tinged or deep purple; spathe ovoid-lanceolate, 1–2.2 by 0.5 cm, apex rostrate, ca 2 mm long, gaping at anthesis and then soon closing, green or pinkish-tinged or deep purple, persistent late into fruit development; spadix tapering-cylindrical, ca 2.2 by 0.5 cm, equalling spathe, stipitate; stipe ca 2 mm long; pistillate flower zone ca 4 by 2 mm; ovary ovoid-globose, ca 1 mm diam., with an associated clavate staminode ca ⅓ height of the ovary; style short; stigma capitate, ovary pale green to purple, staminode white; staminate flower zone ca 1.3 cm by 3 mm; staminate flowers ca 0.75 mm diam., each with two stamens, connective very briefly rostrate, white. description: Small, clump-forming, evergreen, rheophytic, barely aromatic herb to 15 cm. Stem initially erect, but soon creeping, 0.5–1 cm thick, oldest parts leafless. Leaves many together; petioles 5–16 cm; petiolar sheath 3–4 cm, margins scarious; leaf blade lanceolate to very narrowly elliptic, rarely linear, 4–18 cm by 1.5–5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to acuminate, with a 2–3 mm tubular mucro, thinly coriaceous; primary lateral veins 4–6 diverging from the lower half of the midrib at 25°–30°; interprimary veins much finer, striate; secondary venation almost invisible, very weakly tesselate. Inflorescences 1–5 together; peduncle 1–2.5 cm; spathe oblong-lanceolate, ca 2.5 by 0.5 cm, apex long-acuminate to rostrate, ca 4 mm long, spathe barely opening at anthesis and then soon closing, medium to pinkish green; spadix cylindrical, ca 1.7 by 0.3 cm, shorter than spathe, stipitate; stipe ca 2 mm long, obliquely inserted onto spathe base; pistillate flower zone ca 5 by 2 mm; ovary depressed ovoid-globose, ca 1 mm diam., without associated staminodes; staminate flower zone ca 1 cm by 2 mm; staminate flowers each with two stamens, ca 2 mm diam., white. description: Moderate to large, robust, strongly aromatic (mango resin), stemless to erect to decumbent-stemmed herb to 1 m. Stem erect, later decumbent, 1–3 cm diam., usually covered with leaf bases for the terminal half, older portions naked or with semifibrous petiole and cataphyll remains. Leaves several together; petioles up to 45 cm long, pale to mid-green to deep red, with darker longitudinal streaks to ca 1.5 cm long; petiolar sheath 7–11cm, margins membranous, persistent, often darker coloured or red when petiole green; leaf blade ovate-sagittate, 15–45 by 10–22 cm, base sagittate, the sinus very wide (up to ca 7 cm) but shallow, apex acute, with a ca 2 mm tubular mucro, coriaceous, mid-green above, paler green to deep red below, drying distinctively dark brown; venation of posterior costae with ca 4 primary lateral veins arising more or less together, anterior costa with 5–9 primary lateral veins and a similar number of finer, interprimary veins diverging from the midrib at 30°–45°; secondary venation striate. Inflorescences 1–7 together; peduncle 10–18 cm, erect (developing and floral) to declinate (after anthesis and fruiting), coloured as for petioles; spathe oblong, 8–14 cm long; spathe limb gaping at anthesis, then closing again and persistent into fruit, greenish white internally, yellowish to medium red-white externally, usually with darker spotting on the base and dorsal surfaces associated with extrafloral nectaries; spadix tapering-cylindrical, 8–13 cm, barely exceeding spathe, short stipitate; stipe ca 2–4 mm, pale green; pistillate flower zone ca.3 by 1 cm, weakly fusiform; ovary depressed ovoid-globose, ca 1 mm diam., with an associated, very slender-stalked, globose-clavate topped staminode equalling the height of the ovary; ovary very pale green; stigma capitate, sessile, equalling the ovary diam., pale yellow-white, staminode ivory; staminate flower zone 5.5–6 cm by 1 mm, tapering fusiform; staminate flowers 4–5-androus, rhombohexagonal in plan view, ca 3 by 2 mm, overtopped by a large connective, ivory white, lowermost flowers sterile. Fruits ovoid, pale green, ca 3 mm diam.

description: Medium to large, usually robust, colony-forming, strongly aromatic (pinene) helophyte to 1 m tall, but usually less. Stem hypogeal, stoloniferous, 1–3 cm thick. Leaves few together; petioles 10–25 cm, rather spongy, deep green; petiolar sheath 3–4 cm, margins membranous; leaf blade very variable, ranging from linear-lanceolate through ovate-lanceolate to strongly hastate, 6–35 by 3–20 cm, base cuneate to truncate to cordate or strongly hastate, apex blunt to long acuminate, with a 2–5 mm tubular mucro, rubbery-coriaceous, deep green; primary lateral veins 4–11 per side; interprimary veins much finer, striate; secondary venation almost invisible. Inflorescences 1–2 together; peduncle 15–25 cm, green to purple-brown; spathe with a moderate constriction between the lower part and the spathe limb, 8–14 cm long; lower part ovoid-ellipsoid, 2–4 by 1–1.5 cm; spathe limb lanceolate to lanceolate-elliptic, 6–9 by 2–3.5 cm, spreading at anthesis, then closing again; spadix tapering-cylindrical, 6–10 cm, subequalling spathe, stipitate; stipe ca 1 cm long; pistillate flower zone 1.5–3 by 1 cm; ovary depressed ovoidglobose, ca 1 mm diam., with an associated clavate staminode ca equalling the height of the ovary; stigma sessile, capitate, ovary pale green, staminode white; sterile interstice ca 1 cm long, with a few scattered staminodes, these ovoid, compressed, white, axis of interstice pale green; staminate flower zone 4.5–5.5 cm by 3 mm; staminate flowers rhombohexagonal in plan view, ca 1–2 mm diam., each with two stamens overtopped by a large connective, white. Fruits ripening dull yellow.

description: Small, solitary to weakly clumping evergreen, weakly aromatic herb to 40cm. Stem erect, older plants decumbent to creeping, 1–2 cm thick. Leaves few together; petioles 12–32 cm, green or deep purple or deep red, even in the same population; petiolar sheath 7–9 cm, margins membranous, apical portion decurrent or sometimes weakly truncate-auriculate; leaf blade ovate-triangular to cordate-hastate-triangular, 6–22 cm by 4–14 cm, base truncate to roundedtruncate to weakly hastate, apex long acuminate, with a 2–3 mm tubular mucro, coriaceous; primary lateral veins 4–9 per side, frequently drying much darker than the surrounding leaf blade; interprimary veins much finer, striate; secondary venation almost invisible. Inflorescences 1–4 together; peduncle 7–11cm, colour as for petioles; spathe oblong-lanceolate, 4–6 by ca 1.5 cm, apex apiculate, ca 2 mm long, spathe gaping at anthesis and then soon closing, deep red; spadix tapering-cylindrical, ca 5–6.5 by 0.5–0.7 cm, subequalling spathe, stipitate; stipe ca 4 mm long, reddish tinged; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, ca 1.7–2.2 cm by 4 mm; ovary depressed ovoid-globose, ca 0.5 mm diam., pale green, tinged pinkish red, with an associated clavate staminode ca equalling the height of the ovary, staminode ivory; stigma briefly slenderstipitate, capitate, smaller than the ovary diam., pinkish; staminate flower zone 4–4.5 by ca 1 cm, tapering fusiform; staminate flowers 4-androus, rhombohexagonal in plan view, ca 1 by 1.5 mm, stamens overtopped by a large connective, ivory, lowermost flowers sterile. Fruits not seen.

description: Clump- and colony-forming, stoloniferous, evergreen, prickly helophytes. Stem thick, aculeate or unarmed, decumbent, green, epigeal or submersed, internodes relatively long or short. Leaves several together; petiole long, aculeate, weakly pulvinate apically, petiolar sheath relatively short; leaf blade sagittate to hastate-sagittate when juvenile, adult leaf blade deeply pinnatifid in anterior division, posterior divisions pedatifid, sometimes simple, adult blade rarely entire, or bipinnatifid (the last not in Thailand) with major veins aculeate on lower surface; primary lateral veins pinnate in anterior division, pedate in posterior divisions, primary lateral veins of each pinna forming submarginal collective vein in pinnatifid leaves, or running into marginal vein in simple leaves; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle subequal to petiole, aculeate; spathe linear, very long and narrow and opening only basally (L. spinosa) or broader and opening terminally (not in Thailand), very thick and spongy, spirally twisted or not, marcescent or deciduous, basal part enclosing spadix, gaping at anthesis, or remaining closed and the spathe gaping terminally; spadix shortly cylindrical, obtuse, sessile; flowers bisexual, perigoniate; tepals usually 4, more rarely 6, hooded; stamens 4(–6), free; filaments broad, connective slender; thecae ellipsoid, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; gynoecium ovoid to ellipsoid; ovary 1-locular; ovule 1, anatropous, funicle very short, placenta apical; stylar region well developed, shortly attenuate to cylindrical; stigma discoid-hemispherical. Fruit a quadrangular, apically densely muricate to spinose or smooth (the latter not in Thailand) 1-seeded berry, green or dull purple when ripe. Seed large, compressed-obovoid, testa thin, brown, hard, somewhat rugose, embryo large, somewhat curved.</br></br>Two species of medium to moderately large, prickly helophytes with mostly compound leaves and long-persistent inflorescences. One species in Thailand, frequently persisting in disturbed areas as a result of local use as a green vegetable.</br></br>Immediately distinctive by almost all vegetative parts prickly, it is the only Thai indigenous aroid so armoured, although related genera (Cyrtosperma and Podolasia) occur in Peninsular Malaysia. The prickly green fruits are also diagnostic.

description: Robust, colony-forming, stoloniferous, evergreen helophytes to 1.5 m. Stem thick, prickly, rarely unarmed, erect to decumbent, epigeal or submersed, green. Leaves several together; petiole to 100 cm long, aculeate, weakly pulvinate apically, sheath relatively short; leaf blade (juvenile) sagittate to hastate-sagittate, (adult) deeply pinnatifid in anterior division, with posterior divisions pedatifid, sometimes simple, 18–75 by 6–35 cm; major veins aculeate on lower surface; primary lateral veins pinnate in anterior division, pedate in posterior divisions; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle subequal to petiole, to 45 cm tall, aculeate; spathe linear, 25–55 by 2–4 cm, very long and narrow, thick and spongy, spirally twisted, marcescent, basal part enclosing spadix, gaping at anthesis, yellow to purple or brownish; spadix shortly cylindrical, 4–5 by 1 cm, obtuse, sessile; gynoecium ovoid to ellipsoid, ca 2 mm diam. Infructescence stoutly cylindrical, to 7 by 2 cm; fruits quadrangular, apically densely muricate to spinose, ca 1.5 cm diam., green when ripe.

description: Small to medium-sized, evergreen, obligate rheophytes. Stem erect or decumbent, usually more or less condensed. Leaves several; petiole semiterete to canaliculate on upper side; petiolar sheath short with long, marcescent ligule; leaf blade elongate-lanceolate to elliptic or oblanceolate, coriaceous, basally cuneate, apex with tubular mucro; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into distinct marginal vein; secondary laterals and higher order venation either parallel-pinnate or tessellate. Inflorescence one per module, emerging orthotropic, maturing (prior to the onset of anthesis) anatropic; peduncle subequal to or longer than petiole; spathe stoutly ellipsoid, not constricted, usually pink, rarely white, lower part persistent and cup-like, upper part inflating and then gaping at anthesis, soon-caducous, cuspidate to acuminate, often with a pronounced terminal rostrum becoming reflexed at anthesis, interior frequently with one to several pronounced crests, especially in the distal part; spadix sessile with oblique insertion, often with staminodes basally; pistillate flower zone cylindrical; pistils connate into a synandrium, or free but cohering to neighbouring ones; ovary 1-locular; ovules many, placenta 2–4, parietal; stigma ± sessile, usually as broad as ovary and more or less contiguous with adjacent ones; staminate flower zone contiguous with pistillate, cylindrical to ellipsoid, equal in thickness to pistillate, obtuse; stamens arranged in pairs or irregular, free, compressed, anthers truncate, connective ± flat or expanded apically or with conical beak (the last not in Thailand), overtopping thecae; thecae oblong-ellipsoid, dehiscing by apical pore; appendix absent. Infructescence a cluster of berries subtended by the obconical spathe base carried on an erect peduncle, spadix above fruiting portion degrading and shed entirely soon after fertilization; berry obovoid to subcylindrical, small, green, either fused into a syncarpium (most species), or free but cohering to adjacent berries (not in Thailand). Seed numerous, elongate-ellipsoid to cylindrical, with long, curved micropylar appendage, testa slightly costate, embryo elongate, endosperm copious.</br></br>Eleven species in Malesia, the majority (nine) endemic in Borneo. One species in Thailand.</br></br>Piptospatha is defined by the combination of shedding spathe limb, thecae lacking a horn, parietal placentation, an erect splash cup, fruits either fused into a syncarpium (most) or free but cohering (P. insignis N.E.Br.), and the presence of a micropylar appendage on the seed.

description: Rheophytic herb 10–40 cm tall. Stem short, condensed, 2–4 by 0.7–1 cm; roots thick, extensive and tough, 1.5–2 mm diam., with many thinner roots of second order. Leaves few to several together; petiole 6–15 cm long, 1.5–2 mm diam., canaliculate on upper side, sheathing only at the extreme base, the wings extended into a narrow ligular portion 3–7 cm long; leaf blade coriaceous, adaxially dark mid-green, paler abaxially, elliptic (to oblong elliptic) 10–26 by 1.5–7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute and shortly apiculate for 1–1.5 mm, margins weakly to strongly crispate especially distally; midrib and primary venation very prominent abaxially, drying pale orange to straw-coloured; primary lateral veins 5–8(–10) on each side, running to a thick marginal vein; secondary venation distinctly finer than primaries; tertiary venation forming a obscure tessellate pattern. Inflorescence solitary (sometimes 2–3 in series but alternating with foliage leaves); peduncle erect, 3–16 cm long; spathe nodding at anthesis, narrowly ovoid, ca 3 cm long, apically beaked for ca 4 mm, lower part dull pale green, limb creamy white to white, caducous; spadix ca 2 cm long, shortly stipitate; stipe adnate to the spathe; pistillate flower zone thickly discoid, about as broad as the ovary (dry), papillate, not contiguous with neighbouring stigmas (dry); interpistillar staminodes confined to a small group or irregular whorl at the base of the pistillate zone, individually stipitate, flat-topped, about as long as the pistils, ca 0.5 mm diam.; sterile interstice absent; staminate flower zone fertile to apex, bluntly ellipsoidsubcylindrical, ca 1 by 0.5 cm; stamens truncate, more or less flat-topped to somewhat rounded, narrowly rectangular-elliptic, anthers ﬁnely and densely pubescent, ca 0.8 mm across. Fruiting spathe obconical, green; berries yellowish when ripe, in a more or less hemispherical group ca 1.5 cm diam., obovoid, 2.2–2.4 by 1.5 mm, with persistent, apical stigma remnant. Seeds several, subcylindrical, ca 1–1.2 mm long; testa slightly ribbed, brown, with a prominently curved micropylar appendage.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Small, free-floating, stoloniferous, evergreen herb with pendent feathery roots. Stem very short, acaulescent, stoloniferous. Leaves several in a rosette up to 30 cm across but often much less, densely pubescent; petiole very short, almost absent, sheath very short, ligulate, very thin, scarious at base; leaf blade somewhat spongy, obovate-cuneate to obovate-oblong, up to 10 by 7 cm, apex rounded, truncate or retuse; midrib absent; primary veins subparallel, all arising from base, diverging slightly and running into margin near apex, strongly prominent on lower surface, higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, very small, much shorter than leaves and partially hidden among leaf bases; peduncle 3–5 mm, pubescent; spathe pubescent externally, glabrous within, somewhat constricted centrally, ca 10–12 by 5–7 mm, lower margins connate and adnate to ovary wall together forming tube, free margins between tube and spathe limb folded between stigma and staminate organs forming a partition between an upper staminate partial chamber and a lower pistillate one, limb erect, ovate, expanded, acute-acuminate; spadix shorter than spathe, mostly adnate to spathe, ca 5–7 mm, only the apical staminate zone free; pistillate flower zone bearing a single gynoecium at base and a thin, green, pouch-shaped flap just below spathe partition; ovary obliquely adnate to spadix axis, ovary ovoid, ca 1 mm diam., 1-locular; stylar region attenuate, bending inwards towards staminate flowers; stigma small, discoid-subcapitate; staminate flower zone subtended by a thin, marginally lobed, green, annular flap, composed of a basally naked spadix axis supporting a single whorl of 2–8 flowers with the naked axis sometimes extending a little beyond; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; synandrium composed of 2 connate stamens, ca 2 mm diam., subtended by a thin, marginally lobed, green, annular flap; thecae dehiscing by a single apical slit. Fruit a thin-walled, utricular, many-seeded, ellipsoid berry, irregularly breaking up and decaying to release seeds. Seed barrel-shaped, ± subtruncate and excavated at apex and base, testa thick, reticulate-alveolate, thicker and with operculum at micropylar end.</br></br>A single species of free-floating aquatic stoloniferous evergreen herbs. Pistia stratiotes, the only accepted species, has a very considerable synonymy, with the formerly recognized ‘species’ separated on trivial characters.

description: Small to very large, slender to rather robust primary hemiepiphytes. Stems rather ‘woody’, lower branches rooting, upper ones free and pendent in most species, buds of lateral shoots sometimes perforating the leaf sheath or ± infra-axillary. Leaves distichous, juvenile plants of some species with a shingle form; petiole pulvinate apically, either broad, completely flattened and usually auriculate apically, or morphology normal with a long sheath, sometimes sheath reduced to a pair of hyaline ridges; leaf blade linear-lanceolate to ovate or elliptic, sometimes oblique; primary lateral veins either mostly arising near base of blade, long arcuate, and running into marginal vein near apex, or pinnate, weakly differentiated, forming submarginal collective vein, 1–2 marginal veins also present and these crossing the primary lateral veins to produce a distinctive ‘pothoid’ venation; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence morphologically axillary or infra-axillary, solitary or forming short free, very rarely elongating and rooting, synflorescences of several inflorescences, bearing 4–6 or more rigid, coriaceous cataphylls at the base; peduncle very short to very long, sometimes reflexed; spathe ovate to linear, rarely very long, persistent into fruiting; spadix globose, ovoid, cylindrical, ellipsoid or obovoid, sessile to long-stipitate, densely or laxly flowered; flowers bisexual, perigoniate; tepals 4–6, usually arched, free or partially to completely connate; stamens 4–6, free; filaments oblong, flattened, connective slender; thecae ellipsoid, dehiscing by slits; gynoecium with ovary ovoid-oblong or depressed, (2?–)3-locular; ovules 1 per locule, anatropous, funicle short, placenta axile at base of septum; stylar region sometimes as broad as ovary; stigma discoid-hemispherical to umbonate. Fruit an ellipsoid to ovoid 1(–3)-seeded berry, usually red or rarely whitish or dull purple when ripe. Seed ellipsoid, testa smooth, embryo large, endosperm absent.</br></br>Approximately 75 species ranging from Madagascar to India, the subtropical eastern Himalayas, throughout subtropical and tropical Asia into western Oceania and tropical eastern Australia.</br></br>Eight species in Thailand, none endemic.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Small to very large, slender to robust, homeophyllous root-climbing hemiepiphyte to 10 m. Stem weakly four-angled, slightly compressed or terete in cross-section, mid-green, becoming greyish brown with age; fertile shoot often branching to three or more orders. Leaves many; petiole broadly winged, obovate-oblong to linear-oblong or elongate-triangular, 5–14 by 0.5–2 cm, with 2–3 secondary veins and numerous veinlets per side, base decurrent to clawed, apex truncate, rounded or auriculate; leaf blade ovate to elliptic or lanceolate, 3–21 by 1.5–25 cm, leathery, drying chartaceous. Flowering shoot much abbreviated, arising from most of the midto distal leaf axils of fertile shoots, bearing a minute prophyll and a few 3–15 mm sequentially longer cataphylls. Inflorescence 1–2 together; peduncle rather stout, 3–25 by 1.5–2.5 mm, erect to variously curved, green to brown-tinged; spathe 4–12 by 4–10 mm, ovate, concave, margins in-rolled, base cordate, clasping and slightly decurrent on the peduncle, apex hooded to recurved, acute to subacute with a rather stout mucro, greenish white to green, occasionally faintly purpletinged, somewhat waxy; spadix stipitate; stipe terete in cross-section, 5–10 by 1–1.25 mm, erect, straight, green; fertile portion globose to ovoid, 3.5–13 by 3–10 mm, pale green to white; flowers ca 1–2 mm diam. Infructescence with 1–5 berries; fruit obclavate to ovoid or ellipsoid, 1–1.8 by 1–1.4 mm, mid-green ripening to scarlet, often with basal chartaceous tepal remains.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Slender, heterophyllous, root-climbing hemiepiphyte to 3 m. Stem (juvenile) ca 1.5 mm diam., terete to slightly angled in cross-section, shingle-leaved; stem (mature) ca 6 mm diam., terete in cross-section. Leaves scattered, spreading; petiole slender, canaliculate, rounded abaxially, 2–10.5 cm by 1–6 mm, base decurrent, apex prominentlypulvinate; petiolar sheath distinct, prominent, erect, apically ligulate in young growth, ligule later disintegrating, base amplexicaul or decurrent to almost free; leaf blade broadly to narrowly oblong-elliptic, 8–26 by 1.6–9.5 cm. Flowering shoot much abbreviated to rarely rather elongated through reiteration, leafless or occasionally bearing developed but undersized foliage leaves. Inflorescence solitary on each reiterating flowering shoot but many such shoots arising sequentially; peduncle somewhat robust, strongly curving or straight with the inflorescence held erect, 2.5–6.5 cm by 1–4 mm, mid green; spathe linear-triangular to narrowly oblong, 3.4–6.7 by ca 1 cm, base rounded, annulately inserted onto peduncle, apex acuminate, slightly rough to smooth, pale brown tinged reddish pink; spadix stipitate; stipe 3–19 by 1–2 mm, terete; fertile portion 3.5–13.5 cm by 0.5–3 mm, very slender-cylindrical, occasionally sterile at the tip, pale greyish pink, older inflorescences blackish red; flowers 3 by 2.1 by 1.6 mm diam., widely scattered, arranged in a lax spiral along the spadix. Infructescence not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Moderate, slender, heterophyllous, root-climbing hemiepiphyte to 7 m. Stem (juvenile) ca 3 mm diam., terete in cross-section, shingle-leaved; stem (mature) to 8 mm diam., terete in cross-section. Leaves dense; petiole slender, 4–12 cm by 2–2.5 mm; petiolar sheath extending to pulvinus, clasping basally on juvenile and mature sterile shoots, prominent and sheathing to ⅘ of its length on fertile shoots; leaf blade ovate to elliptic or lanceolate, 5–25 by 2.5–9 cm, stiffly chartaceous, air-drying dull green with the midrib pale yellow and prominently raised. Flowering shoot elongated, leafy, arising from most of the mid- to distal-most leaf axils of fertile shoots. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle reflexed by ca 90° at the base with the inflorescence held inverted beneath the shoot, 2–5 cm by 1.5– 2.5 mm, stout, yellow to orange-brown; spathe ovate, deeply cucullate with the apex acute, 4–10 by 2.5–6 cm, base slightly decurrent on the peduncle, deep purple inside and out, softly leathery and rather prominently net-veined; spadix sessile, cylindrical, 2.5–7 cm by 3–8 mm, deep glossy purple-brown; flowers ca 1 mm diam. Infructescence not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
