description: Moderate, robust, (heterophyllous?), root-climbing hemiepiphyte to 8 m. Stem (mature) to 6 mm diam., terete in cross-section; fertile shoots seldom branching, stem of fertile shoot to 4 mm diam., densely clothed with leaves. Leaves dense; petiole slender, 3–7 cm long; petiolar sheath somewhat prominent, extending to just below apical pulvinus, basally clasping, apically briefly auriculate to slightly ligulate; leaf blade oblong-elliptic, often falcate, unequal, occasionally quite strongly so, 10–34 by 2.5–10 cm, base rounded, apex acute to acuminate, very briefly tabulate, stiffly but thinly chartaceous, air-drying dull greenish. Flowering shoot arising from below the leaf axils of fertile shoots, abbreviated, usually leafless but with 1–several well-developed cataphylls, very occasionally with one or more fully developed but reduced leaves. Inflorescence solitary but flowering shoots almost always reiterating and thus several inflorescences at varying degrees of developmental maturity often present; peduncle moderately stout, 3–5 cm by 2–3 mm, erect or curving and ultimately ascending with the inflorescence held erect, dull green; spathe lorate, 2.5–10 cm by 5–15 mm, spreading, base auriculate, auricle margins inrolled, barely decurrent on the peduncle, apex obtuse, acuminate, mid green; spadix stipitate; stipe 8–15 by ca 2 mm, slender, terete, lime green; fertile portion 5–6.5 cm by 3–4 mm, cylindrical to tapering slender-cylindrical, straight to slightly curved, base unequal, creamy yellow; flowers ca 1.5 mm diam. Infructescence with numerous berries; fruit 1–1.5 cm by 5–8 mm, obclavate to ellipsoid, ripening deep scarlet, with basal chartaceous tepal remains.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Pothos leptostachyus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 258. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Large, robust, homeophyllous, root-climbing hemiepiphyte to 15 m. Stem (juvenile) to 8 mm diam., weakly angled or subterete in cross-section; stem (mature) 12 mm diam. Leaves dense; petiole broadly winged, oblong to obovate-oblong, 5–14 cm by 5–15 mm, with 4–5 secondary veins per side, base decurrent to clawed, apex truncate, rounded or auriculate; leaf blade ovate to elliptic or lanceolate, 3–18 by 1.5–20.5 cm, with 2–4 intramarginal veins per side, base rounded to cuneate, apex attenuate-mucronate to acute or attenuate, minutely tabulate, leathery. Flowering shoot much abbreviated, arising mostly from the middle to distal leaf axils of fertile shoots, sometimes arising on older leafless parts, bearing a minute prophyll and a few 5–35 mm, sequentially longer cataphylls. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle rather stout, 4–10 cm by 1.5–2 mm, erect, dull orange-yellow; spathe ovate, 2.5–3 by 2–2.5 cm, flat to convex, base cordate, clasping the peduncle, apex slightly raised, acute to subacute with a stout mucro, white, somewhat waxy; spadix stipitate; stipe terete in cross-section, 2.5–4 cm by 2–2.5 mm, erect, straight, pale green; fertile portion ovoid-clavate, 1.25–1.5 by 1–1.5 cm, mid-yellow; flowers ca 1–2 mm diam. Infructescence with 1–5 berries; fruit obclavate to ovoid or ellipsoid, 1–1.75 by 1–1.4 cm, deep green ripening to scarlet, epidermis of upper part of ovary roughened in submature fruits, more or less smooth when ripe.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Large moderately robust, homeophyllous, root-climbing secondary hemiepiphyte to 15 m. Stem to 15 mm diam., four-angled or slightly compressed-terete in cross-section; fertile shoot branching to ca two orders, stem to 10 mm diam. Leaves dense; petiole 2–20 cm by 5–20 mm, broadly winged, obovate-oblong to linear-oblong, with 2–3 secondary veins and numerous veinlets per side, base decurrent, apex truncate, rounded or auriculate; leaf blade 2–10 by 1–4 cm, ovate to elliptic or lanceolate with 2 intramarginal veins per side, base rounded to acute, apex attenuate-mucronate, leathery. Flowering shoot much abbreviated, arising from most of the mid- to distal leaf axils of fertile shoots, bearing a minute prophyll and a few 3–10 mm, sequentially longer, cataphylls. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle slender, 3–15 by 0.5–2 mm, erect to spreading, green to purple-tinged; spathe 4–10 by 4–10 mm, ovate, concave, margins flat to slightly concave, base short, apex rounded to acute with a tiny, rather stout mucro, maroon; spadix long-stipitate; stipe terete in cross-section, 10–15 by ca 1 mm, erect, white; fertile portion globose or ovoid to subclavate, 9–12 by 3.5–10 mm, white; flowers ca 1–2 mm diam. Infructescence with 1–5 berries; fruit obclavate, 1–1.75 by 1–1.5 cm, mid-green ripening to deep scarlet.

description: Moderate to rather large, slender to moderately robust, homeophyllous, root-climbing secondary hemiepiphyte to 6 m. Stem 10 mm diam., weakly four-angled or slightly compressedterete in cross-section. Leaves dense; petiole 2–14 cm by 5–20 mm, broadly winged, obovateoblong to linear-oblong, with 2–3 secondary veins and numerous veinlets per side, base decurrent, apex truncate, rounded or auriculate; leaf blade 2–10 by 1–4 cm, ovate to elliptic or lanceolate with 2 intramarginal veins per side, base rounded to acute, apex attenuate-mucronate, leathery. Flowering shoot much abbreviated, arising from most of the mid- to distal leaf axils of fertile shoots, bearing a minute prophyll and a few 3–10 mm, sequentially longer, cataphylls. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle slender, 3–15 by 0.5–2 mm, erect to spreading, green to purple-tinged; spathe 4–8 by 4–7 mm, ovate, concave, margins variously inrolled, base short or somewhat long-clawed, apex rounded to acute with a tiny rather stout mucro, greenish to maroon; spadix stipitate; stipe terete in cross-section, 5–10 by ca 1 mm, erect, the distal part erect to bent through 270°, greenish to maroon; fertile portion globose or ovoid to subclavate, 4–10 by 3.5–10 mm, yellow green to off-white; flowers ca 12 mm diam. Infructescence with 1–5 berries; fruit obclavate, 1–1.75 by 1–1.5 cm, mid-green ripening to deep scarlet.

description: Slender, (heterophyllous?), root-climbing secondary hemiepiphytes. Stem ca 6 mm diam., sub-terete. Leaves dense; petiole slender, 6–9 cm long; petiolar sheath margins inrolled and thus sheath not prominent, extending to just below pulvinus, basally clasping, apically briefly ligulate; leaf blade lanceolate to lanceolate-elliptic, 6–16 by 2–5 cm, base cuneate to obtuse, apex acute to acuminate, very briefly apiculate, stiffly but thinly chartaceous, drying dull greenish; primary lateral veins arising at ca 80°, very fine. Flowering shoot leafy, arising from the distal-most portions of fertile shoots. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle very slender, 4–11 cm by ca 0.75 mm, arching, very rarely reflexed; spathe lanceolate, 4–5 by 0.5–1 cm, spreading to weakly reflexing, base auriculate, auricle margins inrolled, barely decurrent on the peduncle, apex acute to acuminate, dull reddish purple with paler longitudinal streaks; spadix briefly stipitate; stipe ca 2 mm long; fertile portion slender, cylindrical, 5–7.5 cm by ca 2 mm, straight to slightly curved, base unequal, slightly cochleate, creamy yellow; flowers ca 1.2 mm diam. Infructescence with rather few berries, these mostly carried on the basal half of spadix; fruit ellipsoid, 1–1.2 cm by 4–5 mm, with a prominent stigmatic remnant, ripening deep scarlet.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Pothos wallichii . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 261. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Tuber depressed globose to elongate, napiform or with several vertical branches, 5–20 by 3–30 cm, rarely with a few annual, globose offsets. Leaves one or several together; petiole 5–70 by 0.5–3 cm, wholly green or background green to pale brownish, variously spotted with whitish, blackish or dark green spots, these elliptic or elongate, isolated or confluent, with or without a greyish wax layer; leaf blade trifoliolate to highly decompound, central main segment often smaller than lateral main segments, 20–120 cm in diam.; leaflets lanceolate to broadly elliptic, 2–45 by 1–35 cm, margin sometimes sinuous or crisped, apex acute or acuminate, upper surface mid green, sometimes with a white, regularly interrupted line along each side of the main vein, sometimes with a dull bluish waxy layer, usually glossy, lower surface pale green or with a pale grey wax layer. Inflorescence developing alongside the developing leaves or later, 1–3 per season; peduncle coloured as petiole or paler, shorter, as long as or longer than petiole; spathe cymbiform, triangular-ovate, apex slightly hooded or not, 5–20 by 2.5–15 cm, pale green on both sides, turning whitish at staminate anthesis, top acute, base within bearing scattered or numerous tiny verrucae; spadix shorter than or as long as spathe, 4–15 cm long; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, 10–35 by 8–10 mm, flowers congested; ovaries obovoid, slightly depressed, 1.8–2 mm in diam, off white; style very short and thick, 0.1–0.4 by 1 mm, off-white; stigma depressed to subhemispherical, 1–1.5 by 0.4–1 mm, entire, or with a central depression, off-white; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 3.5–8 by 1–1.8 cm, flowers more or less distant, lower ones sometimes more congested; staminate flowers 3–5(–6)-androus; stamens 2–2.5 mm long; filaments free, basally or entirely fused into a column 1–1.5 by 0.5–0.8 mm; anthers free or variously fused within one flower, sometimes all fused forming a disc; appendix stipitate (stipe to 10 mm long) conical, 2–5 cm by 10–15 mm, subacute to obtuse, surface deeply corrugated, separating into rod-like papillae and short sinuous muri, off-white. Fruit an ovoid berry, to 1.5 by 1.3 mm, red.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Pseudodracontium harmandii . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 184. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Tuber depressed globose, subglobose with one or a few short branches or broadly napiform, 5–8 by 3–10 cm, often developing several annual, tiny subglobose offsets, these often remaining in the skin of the previous year’s tuber. Leaves one to several together; petiole 5–40 by 0.5–1.5 cm, brownish, variously spotted with whitish, blackish or dark green spots, these elliptic or elongate, isolated or confluent; leaf blade moderately decompound, central main segment often smaller than lateral main segments, 10–85 cm diam.; leaflets lanceolate to elongate-elliptic, 10–30 by 6–12 cm, acute, upper surface mid green, usually glossy, lower surface pale green. Inflorescence often developing before leaves or later, 1–3 per season; peduncle coloured as petiole or paler, shorter, as long as or longer than petiole, 10–75 cm long; spathe cymbiform, triangular-ovate, slightly hooded or not, 5–15 by 2.5–13 cm, pale green on both sides, turning whitish at staminate anthesis, outside sometimes with scattered small, whitish, orbicular spots, apex acute, short apiculate, base within bearing numerous tiny verrucae; spadix shorter than spathe, 4–12 cm long; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, 5–15 by 8–10 mm, flowers congested; ovaries obovoid, 2–3 mm diam, depressed or slightly conical, off-white, or yellowish at the apex; style almost nil, 0.1 by 0.9 mm, off-white; stigma disciform, 1–2 by 0.5 mm, with a distinct central depression, off-white, smooth or slightly corrugate or minutely echinate; staminate flower zone cylindrical, slightly fusiform or slightly obconical, 3–5 by 1–1.8 cm, flowers more or less distant; staminate flowers 3–5-androus; stamens 2–2.5 mm long; filaments free, basally or entirely fused, column 1–1.5 by 0.5–0.8 mm; anthers free or variously fused within one flower, sometimes all flowers fully synandrous forming a disc; appendix stipitate, stipe 4–10 mm long, conical, 3–5 cm by 12–20 mm, obtuse, surface deeply corrugated separating rod-like papillae and shorter or longer sinuous muri, off-white. Fruit an ovoid berry, pale red.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Pseudodracontium macrophyllum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 186. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Small to large, slender to robust, seasonally dormant herbs. Stem a subglobose tuber. Leaves 1–2 together; petiole smooth, rough or aculeate, mottled, sheath very short; leaf blade tri-partite to ‘dracontioid’, anterior division simple to trifid, segments simple to pinnatifid, posterior divisions simple to bifid to pedatifid, segments then simple to pinnatifid, ultimate lobes decurrent, ovate-elliptic to triangular, acute to acuminate; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into distinct marginal vein; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, appearing before or with leaf; peduncle much shorter than petiole, although predominantly epigeal, similar in appearance and texture to petiole; spathe margins not overlapping, upper spathe strongly hooded, thick, marcescent; spadix much shorter than spathe, conical to ovoid-conoid, stipitate, fertile to apex; flowers bisexual, perigone absent; stamens ca 6 or more per flower, free, crowded densely together with those of neighbouring flowers; filaments oblong, flattened, connective slender; thecae oblong-ellipsoid, dehiscing by apical, pore-like slits; gynoecium elongate-flaskshaped, ovary 1-locular, ovule 1, anatropous to hemianatropous, funicle short, placenta basal to subparietal, stylar region greatly elongated, straight or somewhat curved, projecting well beyond stamens; stigma small, scarcely or no broader than style. Fruit a globose berry, pericarp densely covered with conical prickles or smooth, with conspicuous, persistent style remnant, dark green. Seeds reniform, black or very dark brown, testa hard, thick, verrucose.</br></br>Two species of seasonally dormant tuberous-stemmed geophytic herbs with complex umbrella-like leaves superficially similar to (although ontogenetically quite distinct from) those of Amorphophallus. Despite the overall similarity of Pycnospatha(especially P. arietina) to various Amorphophallus species, they are not at all closely related. Two species in Thailand.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Pycnospatha  . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 262. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Robust, medium to large, tuberous seasonally dormant herb, to 2.5 m tall. Stem an irregular globose tuber 4.5–15 by 2.5–7.5 cm. Leaves solitary to two together, produced after, rarely with, the inflorescence; petiole (adult) 50–130 cm by 6–10 mm, smooth, rough or aculeate, if aculeate then with scattered to rather dense prickles 0.8–1 mm long, greyish green to pale grey, mottled blackish green to reddish brown; petiolar sheath very short, inconspicuous; leaf blade (adult) ‘dracontioid’, up to 60 by 100 cm, anterior division trifid with the central partition bipinnate, posterior segments with secondary and tertiary segments irregularly pinnatifid, all ultimate lobes decurrent, ovate-elliptic to triangular, acute to acuminate, glossy dark green with a slight bluish green sheen. Inflorescence solitary, appearing before or with leaf; peduncle much shorter than petiole, 8.5–18 cm by 8–10 mm, similar in appearance and texture to petiole; spathe strongly hooded, 9–20 by 3–5 cm, margins not overlapping, thick, exterior pale grey with very dense purple speckling, interior deep purple, marcescent following anthesis; spadix conical to ovoid-conical, shortly stipitate, much shorter than spathe, 4–6 by 1–1.5 cm, pale greyish, stained purple; gynoecium with prominent straight style to 5 mm. Infructescence naked or partially enclosed in decaying spathe remains; fruits globose, ca 2 cm diam., pericarp densely covered with conical prickles, with conspicuous, persistent, style remnant, dark green when ripe.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Pycnospatha arietina . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 262. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Slender, small, tuberous seasonally dormant herb, to 50 cm tall. Stem an irregularly globose tuber 2–5 by 2–2.5 cm. Leaves solitary to two together, produced after, rarely with, the inflorescence; petiole (adult) smooth, 20–35 cm by 2–3 mm, green; petiolar sheath very short, inconspicuous; leaf blade (adult) tripartite, to 35 by 16 cm, anterior division oblanceolate, the base much narrowed, the apex rounded and with 2–3 points, posterior segments elliptic-oblanceolate, bases narrowed, apex either 3–5 dentate or divided into three partial, acute lobes, glossy midgreen. Inflorescence solitary, appearing before leaf; peduncle much shorter than petiole, 5–12 cm by 2–3 mm, mainly subterranean; spathe strongly hooded, 3–7 by 1.5–3 cm, lower margins gaping, thick, exterior deep purple brown, interior deep purple, marcescent following anthesis; spadix conical to ovoid-conical, shortly stipitate, 2–3 by ca 0.5 cm, much shorter than spathe, purple; gynoecium with prominent curving-ascending style to 4 mm. Fruits globose, ca 7.5 mm diam., pericarp smooth, with conspicuous, persistent style remnant, dark green when ripe.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Small to medium-sized, seasonally dormant, lithophytic or epiphytic herbs. Stem a subglobose tuber, producing erect to spreading, unbranched or branching stolons which then produce small, ovoid bulbils at nodes, each with numerous, apically revolute or flexuose barbs (the tips of minute cataphylls). Leaves 1–2 together; petioles robust or slender; petiolar sheath relatively short; leaf blade cordate-lanceolate to cordate-ovate, peltate, acuminate, usually thinly membranaceous; basal ribs well-developed; primary lateral veins pinnate, forming submarginal collective vein very close to margin, marginal vein also present; secondary and tertiary laterals arising from the primaries at a wide angle, then arching towards leaf margin and forming inconspicuous interprimary collective veins (‘colocasioid’ venation); higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, appearing before or after leaves; peduncle shorter than petiole; spathe strongly constricted between tube and limb, sometimes with secondary constriction above the spadix, lower spathe with convolute margins, persistent, enclosing pistillate zone and sterile zone of spadix; spathe limb yellow or red (the latter not yet seen in Thailand), longer than tube, fully expanded or remaining convolute and opening only at base, sometimes becoming reflexed, later caducous; spadix sessile or subsessile, much shorter than spathe; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; pistillate flower zone subcylindrical, about half as long as spathe tube, separated from staminate zone by much narrower zone of sterile staminate flowers; pistillate flowers lacking staminodes; ovary subcylindrical to subglobose, 1-locular or partially 2–4– locular at apex, ovules many, placentae 2–4 and parietal or 1 and basal; stylar region very shortly attenuate; stigma discoid-subcapitate or slightly 3–4-lobed; staminate flower zone ellipsoid or subclavate, fertile to apex, obtuse; staminate flowers 2–3-androus, stamens connate into cuneate-clavate, 4–6-sulcate synandrium, fused filaments distinct, synconnectives somewhat excavated at apex; thecae 4–6, oblong to ellipsoid, dehiscing by apical pore-like slits; synandrodia elongated. Fruit an obovoid to globose many-seeded berry. Seed ellipsoid to subglobose, covered by thick, succulent sarcotesta, or testa verruculose to irregularly costate.</br></br>Four species, two in Thailand, neither endemic, R. vivipara throughout the Old World tropics. Remusatia is immediately recognizable by producing elongate, erect to spreading, aerial stolons bearing clusters of barbed bulbils along their length.</br></br>Gonatanthus is currently included in the circumscription of Remusatia. Formerly, it was differentiated on the presence of a lower spathe with constrictions corresponding to the interstice between the pistillate and staminate flower zones and another above the pistillate flower zone, and basal (vs. parietal placentation). Molecular evidence is beginning to indicate that merging the two genera may have been too hasty.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Small to medium, slender, epiphytic or lithophytic, seasonally dormant herb to 25 cm. Stem a globose tuber 1–2.55 cm diam., epigeal, covered with the fibrous remains of petioles and cataphylls, often a few tubers together; stolons numerous, spreading, much branched, 10–20 cm by 1–3 mm; bulbils ellipsoid, 0.5 by 2 mm, barbs recurved, ca 1 mm. Leaves 3–4 together; petiole slender, 15–40 cm; petiolar sheath occupying lower ¼–⅓; leaf blade ovate to oblongovate peltate, 8–23.5 by 7–14.5 cm, acute or slightly acuminate, base shallowly cordate, sinus 5–45 mm wide; basal ribs well-developed; primary lateral veins 4–5 each side, radiating from petiole and pinnately from midrib of main lobe; secondary venation pinnate from primary veins; dull green on both surfaces, areas between primary veins often purple below and/or above. Inflorescences appearing when plants in leaf, usually one per tuber; peduncle 6–10 cm; spathe 14–22.5 cm long, with two constrictions, one between tube and spathe limb and another above the spadix; lower spathe globose, 1–1.5 by ca 1 cm, green; spathe limb 13–21 cm; the lower part of limb separated in two parts by a constriction; lower subglobose, 1.5–2.5 cm, opening to reveal staminate part of spadix, upper narrowly lanceolate apex long-acuminate, 11.5–21 cm by 6–15 mm, membranous, yellow or yellow-green on both surfaces, erect, elongate, fully opening only for a short time (less than 4 hours), then withering; spadix 2–2.5 cm, much shorter than the spathe; pistillate zone 5.5–7.5 by 3.5–4.5 mm, with 3–4 whorls of staminodes at top and 1–2 whorls at base, ovary globose-ellipsoid, green; stigma capitate, paler; sterile interstice slender, 4–5 mm, tapering upwards, covered with elongated synandrodes, yellow; staminate flower zone clavate, ca 10 by 4 mm, violet to purplish white; synandria 0.6 by 1 mm, violet to purplish white. Fruiting spathe ellipsoid, splitting to reveal globose berries ripening red.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Medium to large, generally rather robust, epiphytic, lithophytic, rarely (in Thailand) terrestrial, seasonally dormant herb to 75 cm. Stem a depressed globose tuber 3.5–5 cm diam., partially epigeal to hypogeal, generally covered with the fibrous remains of petioles and cataphylls, often several tubers together; stolons stout, erect, simple or little-branched, 20–40 cm by 5 mm; bulbils ellipsoid, 0.5 by 2.5 mm, barbs recurved, ca 1.5 mm. Leaves few together; petiole stout, 19–45 cm; petiolar sheath occupying lower ¼; leaf blade oblong-ovate to ovatecordate, peltate, 11–33 by 7–20 cm, apex acute, base shallowly cordate, sinus 1.5–3 cm wide, basal ribs well-developed; primary lateral veins pinnate, forming submarginal collective vein very close to margin; secondary and tertiary laterals veins arising from the primaries at a wide angle; higher order venation reticulate, glossy on both sides green above, paler green abaxially. Inflorescences appearing when plants leafless, usually one per tuber but, in multi-tuber plants, many inflorescences developing simultaneously; peduncle 6–12 cm, subtended by 4 or more cataphylls, 3 by 15 cm long, concealing peduncle; spathe 8–16 cm long with a single constriction between the lower spathe and spathe limb; lower spathe ellipsoid, 3–5 by 1.3–2 cm, green; spathe limb obovate, acute, apiculate, narrowed to base, 5–11 by 5–9 cm, rather thick-textured, bright yellow, initially erect, then soon reflexed; spadix 3–4 cm, much shorter than the spathe, sometimes staminate zone barely exserted from the lower spathe; pistillate flower zone 1.5–2 cm by 7–9 mm, with 3–4 whorls of staminodes at apex and 1–2 whorls at base; ovary globoseellipsoid, green; stigma capitate, paler; sterile interstice slender, 1.1–2.5 cm, tapering upwards, covered with elongate synandrodes; staminate flower zone clavate-cylindrical, 1.5–2.2 cm by 4–7 mm, yellowish; synandria 2 by 3 mm, white. Fruiting spathe ellipsoid, splitting to reveal globose berries ripening red.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Moderate to very large or gigantic, slender to very robust secondary hemiepiphytic, rarely rheophytic, evergreen herbs with abundant trichosclereids. Stem root-climbing, less often prostrate, compressed terete to rectangular in cross-section, often producing long flagelliform shoots with reduced cataphylls and abundant dimorphic clasping and feeding roots. Leaves several to many, distichous to spiro-distichous and often forming tufts at the tips of active shoots, juvenile shingle plants occurring in some species; petiole pulvinate apically and basally, channelled to carinate, rarely sub-terete; petiolar sheath reaching to the pulvinus in many species, somewhat less often reaching only to half-way along petiole, marcescent to deciduous, sometimes decomposing to conspicuous net-fibrous mass; leaf blade lanceolate or oblong, ± oblique, entire, perforate or pinnatifid to pinnatisect, sometimes very large, lobes often subfalcately narrowed; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into marginal vein, often not differentiated from secondaries; secondary laterals ± parallel-pinnate; higher order venation reticulate, but in some species so deeply embedded in leaf tissue as to be almost invisible. Inflorescence usually solitary, occasionally several produced in a synflorescence, arising either on the main clinging axis or, more commonly, from free lateral shoots; peduncle relatively short; spathe boat-shaped, deciduous to marcescent, rarely persistent (not in Thailand); spadix subcylindrical, conical, clavate, sessile to stipitate, mostly shorter than spathe; flowers bisexual, perigone absent; stamens 4, free; filaments oblong-linear; anthers much shorter than filaments, connective slender; thecae ellipsoid, dehiscing by longitudinal slits; gynoecium obconic-prismatic to oblong, truncate, ovary 1-to partially 2-locular; ovules few to many, anatropous, funicle long, placentae parietal to basal, sometimes axile, partial septa variably intrusive; stylar region well developed, equal to broader than ovary, usually truncate apically, sometimes elongate-conical; stigma broadly elliptic or oblong and then transverse, or longitudinal, or punctate-prominent. Infructescence a many-seeded monsterocarp with stylar region deciduous at maturity, revealing a cavity with red, yellow or white pulp. Seed oblong, testa thin, smooth.</br></br>About 100 species of secondary hemiepiphytic, very rarely rheophytic, evergreen climbing herbs. Rhaphidophora is one of the least well understood aroid genera in Thailand and suffers from inadequate field observations and collections. These often massive plants are difficult to represent on herbarium sheets which often show only the most easily sampled portions. Crucially, many historical types are poorly collected, often ill-preserved and at times mixed. Furthermore, our knowledge of the lianescent aroid flora of most countries neighbouring Thailand is still inadequate.</br></br>For these reasons, and in an attempt to make this account useful in the field, we include all possible Rhaphidophora taxa which may occur in Thailand in the key below, un-numbered, non-bold, italic, while providing descriptions only of those that are definitely known.

description: Small to medium-sized, heterophyllous rheophyte, very rarely short liane, to 75 cm; juvenile plants shingling. Stem smooth, mid- to dark green, with very sparse petiolar sheath fibre; feeding roots densely scaly. Leaves distichous, (juvenile) appressed and shingling; (adult) erect or spreading and scattered on pre-adult shoots, tending to become distally clustered on adult shoots; petiole narrowly canaliculate to carinate, 8–31 by 0.3–1.5 cm, smooth, apical and basal pulvini prominent; petiolar sheath prominent, extending to the apical pulvinus, variably persistent and mostly degrading into semipersistent weak fibres; leaf blade entire in seedling and pre-adult individuals, entire, pinnatipartite or pinnatisect in adult plants, narrowly lanceolate to oblong-elliptic, slightly oblique, 21–51 by 2–23 cm, subcoriaceous to slightly fleshy, base decurrent, apex acuminate with a moderately prominent tubule; midrib prominently raised abaxially, sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, raised abaxially, slightly impressed adaxially; interprimaries sub-parallel to primaries, slightly raised abaxially, ± flush adaxially, often forming a weak reticulum; secondary venation prominently reticulate, slightly raised; tertiary venation a network of broadly spaced tessellate veins arising at ca 90° from the midrib and crossing the primaries and interprimaries. Inflorescence one to three together, subtended by a prominent cataphyll degrading to fibres before anthesis; peduncle terete, 8–12 by 0.2–0.4 cm; spathe narrowly canoe-shaped, stoutly beaked, 6.5–7 by 1–1.5 cm, stiffly fleshy, dirty white at anthesis, soon falling; spadix cylindrical, sessile, inserted perpendicular to peduncle, 4.5–7 by 0.6–1 cm, dull whitish; stylar region rather well developed, mostly rhombohexagonal, ca 1–1.5 by 1–1.5 mm, truncate; stigma elliptic, longitudinally orientated, occasionally almost circular, ca 0.5 by 0.3 mm, often very prominent especially in dried material; anthers exserted at anthesis. Infructescence 7–9 by 1–2 cm, often markedly irregular in outline, mid-green when ripe.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Medium to large, moderately robust, leptocaul homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 20 m. Stems weakly rectangular in cross-section, ca 1–2 cm diam., the angles slightly winged, the surfaces between slightly concave. Leaves distichous on adherent and free shoots, those distal on flowering shoots densely so; petiole deeply grooved adaxially, 3.5–11 by 0.15–0.3 cm, smooth, basal pulvinus well defined, apical pulvinus weakly defined; petiolar sheath very prominent, extending to apical pulvinus, briefly acute-ligulate, very soon drying and falling to leave a continuous conspicuous scar from the petiole base; leaf blade entire, narrowly lanceolate, falcate-lanceolate, 13–30 by 3–8 cm, oblique, very thinly coriaceous and drying papery, slightly glossy adaxially, rather matte abaxially, base subacute, apex acute, with a slight apiculate tubule; midrib slightly raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries, no less prominent, very slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; secondary venation ± obscure in fresh material, visible as a very faint reticulum in dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary, on tips of free lateral shoots, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf; peduncle compressed-cylindrical, 2–3 by 0.15–0.5 cm; spathe broadly cigar-shaped, 4–6 by 1–2 cm, stoutly very short-beaked, stiff fleshy, dull yellow at anthesis, paler internally, soon falling; spadix cylindrical, sessile, 3–5.5 by 1–2 cm, inserted ± level on peduncle; stylar region mostly rhombohexagonal, 1–2 by 1.5–2 mm, truncate; stigma punctiform, raised, ca 0.25–0.3 mm diam. Infructescence 6–8 by 2–2.5 cm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora chevalieri . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 270. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Large, occasionally very large, moderately robust, leptocaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 10 m. Stems rectangular in cross-section, up to 2.5 cm wide, the angles winged, the surfaces between sulcate, the stem twisted to produce a complex series of inter-crossing ridges and channels. Leaves weakly spiralled on adherent and proximal portions of free shoots, densely distichous distally on flowering shoots; petiole shallowly grooved adaxially, 4–7 by 0.2–0.3 cm, smooth, with a slight apical and somewhat prominent basal pulvinus; petiolar sheath prominent, extending to and encircling the apical pulvinus, very soon drying and falling to leave a continuous scar; leaf blade entire, falcate-elliptic lanceolate to falcate-oblong or falcate-oblanceolate, 2.5–35 by 1–10 cm, thickly coriaceous to subsucculent, glossy adaxially, matte abaxially, base sub-ovate to acute or briefly decurrent, apex sub-acute with a prominent apiculate tubule, margins slightly reflexed, this becoming greatly accentuated in dried material; midrib barely raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary lateral veins pinnate, slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries, very slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± invisible in fresh material, barely visible in dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary, on tips of free lateral shoots, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf; peduncle compressed-cylindrical-clavate, 1.7–2.5 by 0.2–0.3 cm; spathe cigar-shaped, stoutly short-beaked, 4–6.5 by 1–1.7 cm, thickly fleshy, dull deep yellow at anthesis, soon falling; spadix cylindrical, sessile, 3.5–6 by 0.5–1.3 cm, inserted level on peduncle, dirty white; stylar region rather well developed, mostly rhombohexagonal, 0.8–1 by ca 1 mm, truncate; stigma punctiform, ca 0.3 mm diam. Infructescence not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora crassifolia . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 271. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Very large, often enormous, very robust, pachycaul, heterophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 20 m or more. Stem robust, 3–5 cm diam., terete. Leaves scattered, each foliage leaf separated from the next by several (up to 7) nodes bearing cataphylls; petiole shallowly canaliculate, 20–40 cm, pulvinus indistinct; petiolar sheath extending ⅔ along the petiole, margins soon marcescent; leaf blade (juvenile) blade rotund, entire, 16 by 13 cm, apex abruptly acute; (adult) oblong-ovate, ovate in outline, irregularly and asymmetrically pinnately cut with the incisions reaching the midrib and individual pinnae separated by a portion of naked midrib, 60–100 by 40–50 cm, pinnae 9–15 per side, those at the mid-leaf 3–5 cm wide, apex truncate with ascending falcate tip, base narrowed, 20 by 3–5 cm, with a strong costa, deep lustrous green adaxially, pale green abaxially. Inflorescence solitary or occasionally paired on tips of lateral shoots; peduncle cylindrical, very robust, 11–20 by 1.5–3 cm, green; spathe oblong-ovate, cymbiform, 17–20 by 10–12 cm, creamy yellow both sides, the lower exterior often deep yellow; spadix cylindrical, 15–16 by 2–3 cm, sessile, base oblique, creamy white; stylar region greyish-green-white sloughing to reveal white or yellow pulp cavity. Infructescence 15–20 by 5–5.5 cm, grey-green. Fruit hexagonal-obconical, 18 by 5 mm, apex with a persistent style.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora decursiva . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 271. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Medium, slender, leptocaul homeophyllous liane to unknown ultimate height. Stems smooth, terete, without prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre. Leaves subdistichously arranged; petiole adaxially basally grooved, 11–19 by 0.2–0.5 cm, smooth, apical pulvinus very prominent, basal pulvinus poorly defined; petiolar sheath very prominent basally, extending about half way along the petiole, soon drying and seemingly persistent; leaf blade entire, lanceolate-falcate, very slightly oblique, 16–20 by 2–2.5 cm, stiffly coriaceous, base cuneate, apex acute, with a prominent apiculate tubule; midrib prominently raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation densely pinnate, slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries and hardly less prominent, slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; secondary and tertiary venation reticulate to sub-tessellate in dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary (always?), subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf; peduncle curving-erect, ca 5 cm long by 1.5–2 mm; spathe stiffly coriaceous, broadly oblong in outline (pressed), the tip obtuse with a stout mucro; spadix cylindrical, sessile, inserted level on peduncle, ca 2.5 by 1.3 cm; stylar region rounded, 1.5–1.7 by 1.6–2 mm, truncate; stigma punctiform, raised, ca 0.7 by 0.8 mm diam.; anthers not seen. Infructescence not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora falcata . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 272. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Large, slender to rather robust, pachycaul, heterophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 10 m. Stem 0.7–2.5 cm diam., terete in cross-section. Leaves scattered, with one foliage leaf at each node except for the proximal part of a branch where the first few nodes bear a prophyll and one or more cataphylls instead of foliage leaves; petiole shallowly channelled, 9–33 cm, apical pulvinus indistinct; petiolar sheath reaching the base of the leaf blade; leaf blade ovate in outline, 11.5–42 by 7.5–24 cm, oblique or shallowly cordate, variously pinnatifid, pinnatipartite or pinnatisectly divided, depending on degree of maturity, pinnae 2–5 (–8) per side, each pinna with three conspicuous primary lateral veins, apex acuminate, base truncate, dull mid-green adaxially, pale to strikingly glaucous-green abaxially. Inflorescence solitary, arising from the tips of free lateral shoots; peduncle 10–25 cm long, spreading, apical portion curved; spathe 4.5–8.5 cm long, oblong-ovate, acuminate apically, opening wide, pale glaucous green in bud, opening pale to mid-yellow, waxy; spadix cylindrical, 4.5–8.5 by 0.8-1.3 cm, sessile, apex truncate-rounded, base slightly tapering, dull cream. Infructescence 12–15 by 3–3.5 cm when ripe, subtended by persistent withered spathe remains early in development, stylar tissue falling to expose ovary cavities with the seeds embedded in copious, pale orange pulp.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora glauca . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 273. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Medium to large, moderately robust, pachycaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 15 m. Stems terete, ca 2 cm diam., mid-green, densely grey-ramentose when young, later glabrous. Leaves clustered at the shoot tips; petiole channelled, the margins sharp, 12–30 cm, pulvini distinct 1–2 cm; petiolar sheath reaching to or just short of the apical pulvinus; leaf blade oblique-oblong, 27.5–45 by 15–30 cm, apex with a 15–20 mm long acumen, base rounded, truncate or subcordate, thinly leathery, midrib and primary veins minutely pubescent; primary lateral veins diverging at a 70°–40° angle from midrib; interprimary veins much less conspicuous; secondary & tertiary veins reticulate. Inflorescences solitary on tips of free lateral shoots, pendent; peduncle pendent, 3–5 cm, subtended by 1–2 cataphylls; spathe oblong-ovate, 8–10 cm long, apiculus 15 mm, spathe thick, outside grey-green to glaucous, inside rich yellow, reflexing and splitting into three parts during pistillate anthesis, then falling; spadix fusiform-cylindrical, 4.5–5.5 by 1.5–1.75 cm, sessile, white with brilliant yellow stigmas at pistillate anthesis; dirty pale yellow at male anthesis, basal-most flowers yellow, waxy. Infructescences stoutly cylindrical, 10–14 by ca 3 cm, pendent from the tips of lateral shoots, stigmas prominent.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora hookeri . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 274. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Very large, occasionally enormous, slender to rather robust, pachycaul, heterophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 20 m; juvenile plants shingling. Stems smooth, light green, with sparse to copious prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre, especially at the stem apices; feeding roots densely ramentose-scaly. Leaves distichous; petiole shallowly grooved, upper part ± terete, 9–65 by 0.2–1.5 cm, smooth, apical and basal pulvinus prominent; petiolar sheath prominent, membranaceous, slightly unequal, extending almost to or reaching the apical pulvinus, short-lived, soon degrading into persistent netted fibres, these eventually falling to leave a prominent, slightly corky scar; leaf blade (juvenile) overlapping in the manner of roof shingles, entire, lanceolate, 5–11 by 3.5–6 cm, base slightly cordate; leaf blade (adult) free, entire, pinnatipartite, pinnatisect or pinnatifid, 14–94 by 10–44 cm, broadly oblong-elliptic to oblong lanceolate, slightly oblique, membranaceous to chartaceous & sub-coriaceous, base truncate and very briefly decurrent, apex acute to acuminate, individual pinnae 1–10 cm wide, frequently perforated basally adjacent to the midrib, thus appearing stilted; midrib very prominently raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, raised abaxially, somewhat impressed adaxially, 2–4 primary veins per pinna; interprimaries sub-parallel to primaries, slightly raised abaxially, slightly impressed adaxially; secondary venation strongly reticulate, slightly raised; tertiary venation invisible. Inflorescence solitary to several together, first inflorescence subtended by a membranaceous prophyll and one or more cataphylls, these soon degrading to netted fibres, subsequent inflorescences subtended by one or more soon degrading cataphylls, the whole forming a mass of developing and open inflorescences and developing infructescences partially concealed by persistent netted cataphyll and prophyll remains; peduncle slightly laterally compressed to terete, 6–26 by 1–1.5 cm; spathe narrowly canoe-shaped, stoutly beaked, 10–30 by 3–5 cm, stiffly fleshy, dull yellow at anthesis, gaping wide at female receptivity and then soon falling to leave a large straight scar at the base of the spadix; spadix cylindrical, sessile, inserted ± level on peduncle, 9–26 by 1.5–2 cm, dull green to dirty white; stylar region rather well developed, mostly rhombohexagonal, 1.5–2 by ca 2 mm, slightly conical; stigma punctiform to slightly elliptic, if the latter then mostly longitudinally orientated, ca 0.3–0.5 by 0.2–0.4 mm; anthers barely exserted at anthesis. Infructescence 14–27 by 3-3.5 cm, dark green ripening to dull orange, stylar tissue abscising to reveal orange ovary cavity pulp.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora korthalsii . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 274. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Small to moderate, somewhat slender, leptocaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 5 m. Stems puberulent-scabrid to asperous, especially on older growth, climbing stems weakly rectangular to ± terete in cross-section, free stems ± terete in cross-section, often branching extensively and growing to moderate lengths, hanging under their own weight, dull brown, without prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre. Leaves weakly spiralled and often sparsely arranged on adherent and proximal portions of free shoots, densely spirally-distichous distally on flowering shoots; petiole grooved adaxially, 4–9.5 by 0.2–0.3 cm, smooth, with moderate apical and prominent basal pulvini; petiolar sheath slightly prominent, extending beyond the apical pulvinus by two ligules, very soon drying and falling in strips to leave a continuous scar from the petiole base, around the top of the apical pulvinus and back to the base; leaf blade entire, narrowly elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate to oblong or oblanceolate, 6–24 by 2–10 cm, very softly coriaceous, upper surfaces slightly glossy, lower surfaces pale satin-matte, drying markedly discolorous, dark brown above, pale brown below, base cuneate to acute or sub-ovate, briefly decurrent, apex acute to ovate-acuminate, with a prominent apiculate tubule; midrib slightly raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, slightly raised abaxially, prominent (dark veins against pale lamina) in dried material; interprimaries parallel to, but much less distinctive than primaries, very slightly raised abaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± invisible in fresh material, barely visible in dried specimens, reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf and a very quickly falling cataphyll; peduncle compressed-cylindrical, 1.5–5 by 0.15–0.4 cm; spathe ovate-elliptic, stoutly long-beaked, 3–5 by 0.4–1 cm, thickly fleshy, exterior minutely puberulent, dull yellowish at anthesis, soon falling to leave a substantial, slightly oblique scar; spadix slender cylindrical, sessile, inserted level on peduncle, 3–3.5 by 0.4–0.5 cm, dull yellow-white; stylar region rather well developed, mostly rhombohexagonal, 1.9–2.4 by ca 2 mm, truncate; stigma punctiform, ca 0.3 mm diam., prominent in dried material; anthers barely exserted at anthesis. Infructescence oblong-cylindrical, 2.5–4 by 1–1.2 cm, ripening dirty white, stylar plates sloughing away to reveal amber coloured pulp and pale grey seeds.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora lobbii . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 276. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Large, occasionally very large, robust, pachycaul homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 20 m. Stems smooth, climbing stems markedly rectangular in cross-section, the angles often winged, the surfaces between slightly convex, free stems spreading, irregularly four-angled in cross-section, sometime irregularly terete, branching little, growing moderate lengths, green, later mid-brown, with very sparse to very copious untidy prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre at the apices of active shoots. Leaves distichous to distichous-spiralled on adherent and free shoots, those distal on flowering shoots densely so; petiole deeply grooved adaxially, 5–23 by 0.25–0.5 cm, smooth, apical and basal pulvini weakly defined; petiolar sheath very prominent, extending to and encircling the apical pulvinus, briefly ligulate, very soon drying and degrading into netted untidy fibres, eventually falling to leave a continuous conspicuous scar from the petiole base, around the top of the apical pulvinus and back to the base; leaf blade entire, elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate or falcate-oblong, 8–43 by 2.5–15 cm, coriaceous, upper surfaces semiglossy, lower surfaces matte, base sub-acute to decurrent, apex sub-acute with a somewhat prominent apiculate tubule, margins very slightly reflexed in dried material; midrib raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries and only slightly less prominent, very slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± obscure in fresh material, visible as a faint reticulum in dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf and sparse to copious netted petiolar sheath, prophyll and cataphyll fibre; peduncle compressed-cylindrical, 10–15 by 0.3–0.5 cm; spathe canoe-shaped, stoutly short-beaked, 12–22 by 2.5–6.5 cm, thickly stiff-fleshy, exterior dull yellow green with black “bruising”, interior white with yellow margins, soon falling at female receptivity; spadix tapering-cylindrical, ± sessile, inserted level on peduncle, 9–10 by 1.5–1.7 cm, cream; stylar region, mostly rhombohexagonal, 1.5–2 by 1.7–2.1 mm, truncate; stigma slightly longitudinally elliptic, raised, ca 0.3 mm diam.; anthers barely exserted at anthesis. Infructescence not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora maingayi . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 277. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Very large to gigantic, very robust, pachycaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte climbing 40 m or more. Stems terete, on flowering shoots 3–4 cm diam., non-flowering shoots somewhat more slender. Leaves dense, spiro-distichous; petiole canaliculate, 50–70 cm; petiolar sheath extending to about half way along petiole, soon marcescent; leaf blade ovate-oblong, 50–90 by 28–50 cm, apex abrupt acuminate, base cordate, very stiffly leathery; primary lateral veins 10–13 each side, diverging at 80°–90° from midrib; interprimary veins much less prominent, striate; secondary and tertiary venation forming a conspicuous reticulum in dry material. Inflorescences in fascicles of up to four per synflorescence on the tips of primary clinging shoots, as synflorescence develops primary axis reiterating, overtopping the synflorescence such that the inflorescence cluster is displaced and appears to be produced laterally; peduncle green, 15–18 by ca 2 cm; spathe oblong-cymbiform, 20–27 by ca 16 cm, very thick, initially gaping, then spreading, greenish white, then light yellow, opening deep yellow internally; spadix cylindrical, 18–25 by ca 2.5 cm, sessile, yellow-green at anthesis, apex obtuse, base oblique; stigma pronounced-punctiform. Infructescence stoutly cylindrical, up to 30 by 5 cm, stylar tissue markedly blue-grey glaucous.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora megaphylla . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 277. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Small to moderate, slender, leptocaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 6 m. Stems smooth, flexuous, climbing stems ± weakly 4-angled in cross-section, with the shorter side somewhat sulcate; free stems somewhat laterally compressed in cross-section, often branching extensively, growing to considerable lengths and hanging under their own weight with flowering tips upturned, without prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre. Leaves weakly distichous and sparsely arranged on adherent and proximal portions of free shoots, moderately densely distichous distally on flowering shoots; petiole grooved adaxially, 3–6 by 0.1–0.25 cm, smooth, with a slight apical and prominent basal pulvinus; petiolar sheath slightly prominent, extending beyond the apical pulvinus by two small ligules, very soon drying and falling in strips to leave a continuous scar from the petiole base, around the top of the apical pulvinus and back to the base; leaf blade entire, narrowly falcate-elliptic to falcate-lanceolate or falcate-oblanceolate, 2.5–16 by 1.2–3 cm, thinly coriaceous, drying pale straw-coloured, base cuneate to acute or sub-ovate, apex acute with a prominent tubule; midrib raised abaxially, slightly raised adaxially; primary venation pinnate, slightly raised on both surfaces, prominent in dried material; interprimaries sub-parallel to, but much less distinctive than primaries, sometimes degrading into weakly reticulate venation, very slightly raised abaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± invisible in fresh material, barely visible in dried specimens, reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf and a very quickly falling cataphyll; peduncle compressed-cylindrical, 3–4 by 0.3–4.5 cm; spathe cigar-shaped, stoutly long-beaked, 3–9 by 1–1.5 cm, thin, dull yellow at anthesis, soon falling to leave a large, straight scar; spadix slender cylindrical, sessile, inserted level on peduncle, 2.5–7 by 0.5–0.6 cm, dull yellow-white; stylar region rather well developed, mostly rhombohexagonal, 1.4–2 by ca 2 mm, truncate; stigma punctiform, ca 0.3 mm diam., slightly prominent in dried material; anthers well-exserted at anthesis. Infructescence oblong-cylindrical, 4.5–7 by 1–2.5 cm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora minor . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 278. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Large, occasionally very large, robust, pachycaul homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 15 m. Stems smooth, rectangular in cross-section, the angles often strongly winged, the surfaces between ±flat, ca 1–3 cm diam. Leaves spiro-distichous on adherent and free shoots, those distal on flowering shoots densely so; petiole deeply grooved adaxially, 10–23 by 0.25–0.5 cm, smooth, apical and basal pulvini weakly defined; petiolar sheath very prominent, extending to and encircling the apical pulvinus, briefly ligulate, very soon drying and falling; leaf blade elliptic to elliptic-lanceolate or falcate-oblong, 8–43 by 2.5–15 cm, coriaceous, glossy adaxially, semi matte abaxially, base subacute to decurrent, apex subacute with a somewhat prominent apiculate tubule, margins very slightly revolute in dried material; midrib raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary lateral veins pinnate, slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries and only slightly less prominent, very slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± obscure in fresh material, visible as a faint reticulum in dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary at tips of free lateral shoots, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf and one or more cataphylls; peduncle compressed-cylindrical, 10–15 by 0.3–0.5 cm; spathe canoe-shaped, 12–22 by 2.5–6.5 cm, very shortly, stoutly beaked, thickly stiff-fleshy, dull yellow, paler internally, falling at female receptivity; spadix tapering-cylindrical, 9–20 by 1.5–2 cm, ± sessile, inserted level on peduncle, cream. Infructescence 9–17 by 1.5–2.5 cm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora montana . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 279. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Medium to large, moderately robust, leptocaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 15 m. Stem terete, 8–12 mm diam. Leaves tending to cluster at shoot tips; petiole shallowly channelled, 10–20 cm; petiolar sheath reaching pulvinus, marcescent; leaf blade oblong-lanceolate to elliptic-oblong-lanceolate, 8–25 by 4–11 cm, apex abruptly acuminate or acute, base broadly rounded to sub-truncate; primary lateral veins many, striate, diverging at 45° from midrib; interprimary veins very slightly less conspicuous; secondary venation reticulate. Inflorescences solitary, terminal on lateral free shoots; peduncle robust, 8–10 cm, erect, upper part recurved, subtended by membranous cataphylls, these linear, 6–7 cm long, early caducous; spathe elliptic-oblong or oblong in outline, 7–9 cm long, gaping and then spreading at anthesis then caducous, dull orange outside, dull orange inside with the base stained yellow, apical rostrum ca 10 mm; spadix cylindrical, 5.5–8 cm long, ca ⅘ of total spathe, 10–2 mm diam., sessile, yellowish white to yellow. Infructescence stoutly cylindrical, 10–13 by ca 3 cm, initially green, later turning dull orange prior to stylar plates sloughing away.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora peepla . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 280. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Large to very large, robust to massive climber. Stems terete, up to 3.5 cm diam. Leaves evenly scattered along climbing stems, although tending to be somewhat clustered towards stem tips; petiole 20–35 cm long, somewhat deeply canaliculate, with pronounced apical pulvinus; petiolar sheath extending ca ⅓ along petiole, soon withering; leaf blade (juvenile) ovate, oblong-ovate or oblong-elliptic, entire and not perforated; (adult) broadly ovate-oblong to almost rounded-ovate, 20–50 by 15–25 cm, acute or usually cuspidate-acuminate and rounded or subcordate at base, simple, unequal sided, entire or irregularly and shallowly lobed, occasionally with large holes and some of the perforations usually extending to the margin. Inflorescence solitary, often displaced by shoot extension and appearing lateral; peduncle 5–18 cm long; spathe coriaceous, oblong, acuminate, 15–20 by 10 cm when expanded, greenish at first, becoming whitish then yellowish or pale pinkish orange, soon withering and deciduous; spadix cylindrical, 10–15 cm by 1.5–2.5 cm diam., pale orange at anthesis; stylar plate conical; stigma punctiform. Infructescence not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora pertusa . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 281. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Medium to large, occasionally very large, moderately robust, leptocaul to semipachycaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 20 m. Stems smooth, climbing stems rectangular in cross-section, the angles often slightly winged and surfaces between slightly concave, free stems rectangular to sub-terete in cross-section, green, later mid-brown, without prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre. Leaves distichous on adherent and free shoots, those distal on flowering shoots densely so; petiole deeply grooved adaxially, 1–8.5 by 0.15–0.3 cm, smooth, apical and basal pulvini weakly defined; petiolar sheath very prominent, extending to and encircling the apical pulvinus, briefly ligulate, very soon drying and falling to leave a continuous conspicuous scar from the petiole base, around the top of the apical pulvinus and back to the base; leaf blade entire, lanceolate-elliptic to falcate-lanceolate, slightly to markedly oblique, 4.5–32 by 1.75–8.5 cm, thinly coriaceous, upper surfaces slightly glossy, lower surfaces semimatte, base sub-acute to briefly truncate, apex acute to slightly attenuate, with a prominent apiculate tubule; midrib slightly raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries and only slightly less prominent, very slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± obscure in fresh material, visible as a faint reticulum in dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf; peduncle compressed-cylindrical, 2–8.5 by 0.15–0.5 cm; spathe narrowly elliptic, very shortly, stoutly beaked, 4.5–7.5 by 1–3 cm, thinly but stiffly fleshy, dull yellow at anthesis, paler internally, soon falling; spadix weakly clavate-cylindrical, sessile, inserted ± level on peduncle, 3–6 by 1–2.5 cm; stylar region mostly rhombohexagonal, 1–2 by 1.5–2 mm, truncate; stigma punctiform, raised, ca 0.25–0.3 mm diam.; anthers exserted at anthesis. Infructescence 6–8 by 2–2.5 cm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora sylvestris . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 281. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Small to medium-sized, rather slender, semipachycaul, heterophyllous liane to 5 m. Stems terete, smooth, without prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath fibre. Leaves weakly spiral-distichous; petiole shallowly grooved, 10–34 by 0.2–0.4 cm, smooth, apical and basal pulvini slightly prominent; petiolar sheath prominent, extending to base of apical pulvinus, soon falling to leave a prominent, slightly corky scar; leaf blade sparsely to ± entirely deeply pinnatipartite to nearly pinnatisect, occasionally with large rhombic perforations adjacent to midrib, 12–42 by 9.5–38 cm, broadly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, thinly coriaceous, base truncate or very weakly cordate, apex acute to acuminate, individual pinnae up to 6 cm wide; midrib prominently raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary lateral venation pinnate, raised abaxially, slightly impressed adaxially; interprimaries diverging from primaries, much less prominent, slightly raised abaxially, very slightly impressed adaxially; secondary venation weakly reticulate, very slightly raised; tertiary venation barely visible. Inflorescence often solitary, occasionally a few together, subtended by two prominent cataphylls, these soon falling; peduncle terete, 2–2.5 by 0.3–0.4 cm; spathe canoe-shaped, 3–3.5 by 0.8–1.5 cm, stiffly fleshy, falling soon after anthesis, white with adherent black cataphyll remnants; spadix cylindrical, sessile, inserted slightly decurrently on peduncle, 3–3.5 by 0.75–1 cm, white; stylar region well developed, mostly rhombohexagonal, ca 2 by 2 mm, truncate, margins deflexed; stigma elliptic, longitudinally orientated, ca 1 by 0.2 mm; anthers exserted at anthesis. Infructescence not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Rhaphidophora tetrasperma . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 282. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant, tuberous, geophytic herbs. Stem a depressed-globose tuber. Leaves entire, sagittate-hastate or pedatisect (only the last in Thailand). Inflorescence simultaneous with or preceding leaves; peduncle short; spathe divided into a connate or strongly convolute basal part with a ± marked apical constriction and a spreading, lanceolate to ovate-triangular spathe limb; spadix as long as spathe, with four zones: a proximal pistillate flowered zone, an intermediate sterile interstice with staminodes all over or only at its base, a staminate flowered zone, and a sessile or stipitate appendix; pistillate flowers unilocular with 1 or 2 (or 3) orthotropous, basal ovules; proximal staminodes clavate, distal ones, when present, irregularly cristate or elongate aristate; staminate flowers with 1–3 stamens opening by slits or pores, connective sometimes prolonged. Infructescence with lower part of spathe caducous or remaining; fruits ovoid, 1 (or 2)-seeded. Seeds with endosperm.</br></br>Eight species occurring from Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Vietnam; three species in Thailand, one endemic.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Sauromatum  . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 283. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Tuberous herb covered with single-celled hairs ca 0.5 mm long. Stem a depressed globose tuber, 1.5–2.5 cm diam., producing numerous, annual, subglobose, angular offsets. Leaf solitary; petiole 20–25 cm; leaf blade pedately 5–7-foliolate; leaflets almost sessile, terminal leaflet elliptic, acuminate, 7–31 by 2.5–10 cm; lateral leaflets elliptic with oblique base, outermost one ca ⅔ the length of the terminal one. Inflorescence appearing alongside the first developing leaf; peduncle very short, 1–1.5 cm long; spathe smooth inside, hirsute outside; lower spathe convolute but lower 1 cm with fused margin, 4 by 2 cm, slightly constricted at the top; spathe limb lanceolate-ovate, laterally incurved, 8–13 by 5–8 cm; spadix shorter than spathe: pistillate flower zone broadly cylindrical-conical, to 6.5 by 10 mm; ovaries subcylindrical, unilocular, ovules 2–3; stigma disciform, white or creamish; sterile interstice to 3.5 cm long, lower 0.5–1 cm densely covered with staminodes, rest naked, grooved; lower staminodes clavate, top obtuse, to 7 mm long, pale pinkish purple or dark brownish purple; staminate flower zone 1–1.7 by 0.8 cm; appendix elongate conical, sessile or subsessile, to 10.5 cm long, to 6 mm diam. at the base, base truncate, surface brown or greyish brown. Infructescence naked, globose, to 4 cm diam.; fruit with distinct angular upper part, 1 by 0.5 cm, style remnant acute, 1 mm long.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Sauromatum hirsutum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 284. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Stem a subglobose to depressed globose tuber, producing annual offsets. Leaves one or a few together; petiole 3–60 cm long, variable in colour, uniform, striped or spotted, ranging from green to purple; leaf blade pedatisect, with 7–13 lobes; lobes elliptic to lanceolate, acute, margin flat or sinuous, entire or occasionally crenate, upper surface mid to dark rich velvety green, with or without reddish main vein or splashed with golden spots along the main vein, lower surface pale to grey green, sometimes with scattered reddish purple spots. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle 2–20 cm long; spathe base convolute, ovoid, occasionally with one or a few shallow keels, top more or less constricted, outside pale or mid green, dull mid to dark brown, with or without a few reddish or blackish brown spots or stripes, inside white or whitish green; spathe limb 6–17 by 4–6 cm, ovate to oblong-ovate, cymbiform, slightly hooded, acuminate to caudate, often keeled at the midrib, outside pale or mid green, dirty greenish, dirty pale brownish, with or without a few indistinct darker spots, inside whitish, pale green, with or without a few scattered blackish purple spots; spadix shorter than spathe; pistillate flower zone cylindrical or slightly conical, 2.5–10 by 4–8 mm; ovary ovoid to oblong-ovoid, unilocular, uni- or bi-ovulate; stigma very small, in a depression of the top of the ovary or ring-like surrounding the depression; sterile zone elongate, narrowly fusiform-conical, 2–6 cm long, 3–7 mm diam. at the base, entirely covered by staminodes; lower staminodes with rhombic, flat base and aristate to clavate process, the latter strongly bent upwards, white, the clavate part yellowish white or occasionally dark red, subbasal staminodes exclusively aristate, strongly pointing upwards parallel to the spadix axis, creamish; upper staminodes fused into vertical ridges with numerous, irregular, short processes, often arranged in ridges, white; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 6–10 by 2–7 mm, upper flowers often sterile and differently shaped; staminate flowers white, the upper ones often sterile and subclavate to spathulate or occasionally aristate; appendix subsessile or more distinctly stipitate, cylindrical or rarely fusiform, 1.5–4.5 cm long, 2–6 mm diam., slightly tapering to the obtuse top, base attenuate to the stipe, surface smooth or strongly corrugate, cream or more rarely greyish brown with purple spots, stipe sometimes ridged-verrucate. Fruits with persistent spathe base; obovoid to ellipsoid, pale green when mature, corrugate and shallowly grooved.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Sauromatum horsfieldii . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 284. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Medium-sized, seasonally dormant herb. Stem a depressed globose tuber to ca 4 by 2.5 cm, producing annual, short, fusiform offsets, these covered by woody scales. Leaves few together; petiole very pale dirty greyish green, with a very faint reddish purplish flush at the base, 23 cm by 7 mm, smooth; leaf blade pedatisect, ca 21 cm diam., 5-foliolate, the basal-most leaflet with a small extra lobe, anterior leaflet elliptic, 13 by 6 cm, acuminate, adaxially dark velvety green, main vein flushed with reddish purple, abaxially paler dirty green, veins (especially in unfolding stage) flushed with reddish purple, slightly glossy, margin with numerous, small undulations and flushed with violet, smallest (basal) leaflets strongly asymmetrical, 8 by 3 cm. Inflorescence appearing with the leaf; peduncle 4 cm by 4–5 mm, smooth, largely subterranean, pale greenish with violet striations; spathe 8.5–13 cm long, coriaceous; lower part 3.5–4 by 1 cm, convolute with a faint, mainly dorsal constriction at the middle, coinciding with a more or less distinct thickened annulus on the interior opposite the middle part of the upper staminodial zone; spathe limb triangular, horizontally flexed, 5–9 by 3–5 cm, acute, exterior lower part dirty greenish with reddish purple flushes, constriction reddish purple and green striate, above constriction whitish greenish with pale reddish purple, tiny spots, base interior with a slippery, shiny, waxy layer, lower half glossy pale green, above constriction dull dirty whitish, limb exterior semiglossy whitish greenish with faint pale purplish spots, interior uniformly dull whitish green; spadix shorter than spathe, 5–8.5 cm; pistillate flower zone broadly conical, 5–12 by 7–11 mm, flowers congested; ovaries angular-globose, 1–1.5 mm, white, with 3 to 4 prominent, narrowly or broadly conical projections (ca 0.5 mm long) around the stigma; stigma in depression between projections, very small, nearly invisible; sterile interstice 15–18 mm, covered with two types of staminodes; staminodes of lower staminodial whorl consisting of clavate/spathulate staminodes, lowermost ones to ca 7 mm long, stalked, top part bent downwards and anvil shaped, others near-sessile, horizontal, clavate part dorso-ventrally flattened and often two-topped, all parts dark purple; upper staminodes contiguous with the lower ones but consisting of only the basal part without any extension, narrowly spindle shaped, to ca 5 by 1 mm, raised, flattened, whitish; staminate flower zone cylindrical, top and base oblique, 10–21 by 4.5–8 mm; stamens ca 1 mm long, narrowly rectangular in cross-section, orangeish yellow, connective very broad, pores rounded or vertically oval, subapical, with a pale violet flush; appendix stipitate, stipe thin, laterally compressed, 4–5 by 2–3 mm, whitish yellow, appendix conical, laterally compressed, directed backwards, base truncate, top obtuse, 15–34 by 8–11 mm, with several small, shallow depressions, otherwise smooth, orangeish yellow.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Sauromatum tentaculatum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 28. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Small to moderate, rarely gigantic, evergreen, terrestrial or lithophytic or rheophytic (the last not in Thailand), odourless or, very occasionally, aromatic herbs. Stem pleionanthic or hapaxanthic, hypogeal or epigeal, sometimes erect or decumbent, rarely root-climbing or scandent. Leaves several to many together, spiro-distichous, rarely distichous; petiolar sheath very short or, more often, less than half the petiole length, sometimes variously auriculate or attached only basally but then with a long apical ligule; leaf blade narrow-elliptic, elliptic, lanceolate, oblanceolate, ovate, obovate, cordate, or cordate-sagittate, mostly glabrous, sometimes pubescent or furnished with coarse trichomes on one or both surfaces, sometimes variegated with paler or silvery green, white or yellow; primary lateral veins pinnate, running into a distinct marginal vein; secondary and tertiary laterals parallel-pinnate; higher order venation transverse-reticulate to tessellate. Inflorescences 1–3 (or more) in each floral sympodium; peduncle shorter than petiole; spathe usually constricted between tube and limb, sometimes only slightly so, rarely not at all, lower spathe convolute, persistent, spathe limb thinner, mostly erect, broadly boat-shaped, gaping and then usually caducous during anthesis, less often persistent, rarely marcescent, usually white to cream, sometimes greenish yellow, very rarely pink, cuspidate to acuminate; spadix shorter than or equalling spathe, lower part consisting of cylindrical to conoid pistillate zone, free or partially adnate to spathe, sometimes bearing sterile organs at the very base, upper part of spadix usually subcylindrical to clavate, either fertile staminate below and sterile terminally, or sterile below and fertile staminate terminally, or sterile below, centrally fertile staminate and sterile terminally, lowermost sterile zone sometimes very laxly flowered, often constricted; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; staminate flower 2–3-androus, stamens very short to long, mostly free; filaments usually well developed, sometimes connate basally, always with distinctive tannin cells (dark in dried specimens), connective mostly rather slender, sometimes thicker apically, anthers truncate, often concave apically; thecae opposite, cylindrical or obconical to ovoid, dehiscing by apical, broadly elliptic, or bilobed (8-shaped) or simple pores; sterile staminate flowers comprising staminodes less compressed than stamens, obpyramidal to clavate, usually truncate, short to long; pistillate flowers a gynoecium sometimes accompanied by 1–4 clavate, rarely peltate staminodes with generally distinctly swollen apices, or with sterile flowers scattered among gynoecia; ovary 1-locular; ovules (1–)few to many, anatropous to hemianatropous, funicle rather long, placentae 1–4, parietal, usually extending from base to apex of locule; stylar region inconspicuous or shortly conoid; stigma discoid to capitate, small to as wide as ovary. Fruit an oblong to globose berry, ripening green or dull yellow or rarely deep red, few- to many-seeded. Seed ellipsoid, testa costate, embryo straight, elongate, endosperm copious.</br></br>A large genus of terrestrial mesophytes, less often rheophytic, evergreen herbs. Superficially similar to Homalomena, but tissues odourless. Schismatoglottis in flower are unmistakeable by the spathe limb shedding at the onset of staminate anthesis. Inflorescences are invariably powerfully fragrant (esterases). Three species in Thailand.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Decumbent herb, tissues stongly aromatic (terpenoids) when crushed. Stems epigeal, pleionanthic, rooting in the internodes, dull dark green, ca 2 cm diam. Leaves 3–6 together; petiole 5–25 cm long, to 6 mm diam., with the margins sharp to minutely winged, minutely hairy and faintly rough, deep dull green; petiolar sheath occupying the lower ½–¾ of petiole, wings membranous, persistent, eventually marcescent; leaf blade broadly ovate to oblong ovate, to ca 20 cm long, base obtuse to auriculate, tip rather abruptly acuminate for ca 1–2 cm, margin irregularly wavy, pale green when young, later slightly glossy dark green adaxially, paler abaxially, somewhat chartaceous; primary lateral veins numerous, slightly prominent adaxially near the midrib, the rest flush, prominent abaxially, ca 1 cm apart, diverging at 60–80°, regularly alternating with lesser interprimaries; secondary venation flush abaxially and adaxially, emerging from the midrib and the basal parts of the primary veins; tertiary venation forming a distinct tessellate pattern abaxially. Inflorescences 1–3 together; peduncle ca 4 cm long, 3 mm diam., erect at and after anthesis; spathe 5–12 cm long, conspicuously mucronate for up to 2 cm, shiny mid-green throughout; lower spathe narrowly ovoid to ovoid, 2–4 by 1–2 cm; spathe limb narrowly lanceolate, separated from the lower spathe by a rather weak constriction, gaping slightly in the upper part, the lower part, like the lower spathe, convolute, rather leathery, persistent shortly after anthesis but eventually yellowing and deliquescent; spadix 4.5–9 cm long; pistillate flower zone 1.5–3 cm long, slightly tapering distally, ca 8 mm thick, obliquely inserted to adnate for ca half its length; ovaries 0.5 mm diam., subglobose with 3–4 conspicuous longitudinal bulges, green; stigma sessile, faintly 3–4-lobed, minutely papillate; interpistillar staminodes absent or very few except for a single ring around the spadix immediately below the pistillate zone, stalked, more or less flat-topped and irregularly polygonal, about twice the height of the pistils, white; sterile interstice 0.5–1 cm long, more or less cylindrical, 4–8 mm thick; staminodes mushroom-shaped, ca twice height of pistils, ca 1 mm diam., white, resembling the interpistillar staminodes; staminate flower zone 1.2–2 cm long, slightly thickening distally (the base corresponding with spathe constriction), 4–8 mm thick, pale yellow; stamens ca 1 mm across, filament slab-like; anther flat-topped; appendix 1.4–3 cm long, tapering to a point, deeper yellow than the staminate zone; appendical staminodes columnar, flat-topped, circular to reniform in outline, ca 1 mm diam., slightly taller than stamens so that appendix slightly but abruptly thicker than male zone. Fruiting spathe erect, rather narrowly urceolate, dehiscing from the base; fruits grey-green.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Stoloniferous herb forming colonies, or clump-forming, 15–60 cm tall. Stems hypogeal, hapaxanthic, 1–2 cm diam. Leaves several together; petiole smooth, ca 5–50 cm long (often less); petiolar sheath for ca ⅓ its length; wings of sheath fully attached, persistent, tapering or, especially in diminutive forms, shortly and bluntly ligular at the apex; leaf blade mostly cordate to sagittate, sometimes oblong-lanceolate, 7–35 by 4–18 cm, usually dull mid green, sometimes variegated with 1–2 bands or irregularly spotted grey-green to yellowish green; midrib somewhat abaxially prominent; primary lateral veins 6–15 per side, irregularly alternating with lesser interprimaries, nearly always raised adaxially towards the midrib, marginally impressed, entirely raised abaxially; secondary venation arising mostly from the midrib, sometimes from the bases of the primary veins; tertiary venation inconspicuous. Inflorescences 1–8 together, with a strong esteric odour at pistillate anthesis; peduncle 2–14 cm, erect at anthesis, then deflected; spathe 3.5– ca 12 cm long; lower spathe narrowly ovoid, ca half the length of the whole spathe, green, often minutely longitudinally ridged and rough; spathe limb differentiated from lower spathe by an abrupt constriction corresponding to the base of the staminate zone of the spadix, at pistillate anthesis much inflated, narrowing and turbinate, the apex conspicuously mucronate, completely surrounding the spadix and gaping ventrally or with the margins loosely overlapping, creamy to pale greenish yellow, caducous immediately after pistillate anthesis; spadix ca ¾ the length of the spathe, narrowly hourglass-shaped; pistillate flower zone about half the length of the whole spadix, sessile, somewhat to markedly obliquely inserted to partially adnate to spathe, ca 5–8 mm diam. below, distally tapering to ca 3–4 mm diam.; ovaries flask-shaped, ca 1 mm by 0.5 mm diam.; stigmas button-like, papillate, raised on a short style; interpistillar staminodes white, mostly conspicuously taller than pistils, few in number, scattered, stalked, clavate, rarely absent in very small forms; sterile interstice between staminate and pistillate zones absent save sometimes for a relative concentration of interpistillar staminodes amongst the distal pistils; staminate flower zone narrowly obconical, approximately half the length of the pistillate zone, distally ca 0.5–1 cm diam., ivory; anthers dumbbell-shaped from above, ca 0.5 by 1 mm, with thecae apically impressed, the connective shorter than to very slightly elevated above the thecae; appendix bullet-shaped to hemispherical, basally nearly always somewhat wider than apex of staminate zone, creamy yellow; appendix staminodes columnar, irregularly polygonal, flat- to slightly round-topped, ca 0.5 mm diam. Fruiting spathe declinate, urceolate.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
