description: Clump- to colony-forming, usually stoloniferous herb, sometimes with individual crowns markedly distant. Stems hapaxanthic, hypogeal. Leaves to 5 together; petiole 15–45 cm long, smooth, adaxially flattened to somewhat channelled, the angles blunt to somewhat acute, but not winged; petiolar sheath in lower ca ¼, wings persistent, membranous, straight to slightly inrolled, to ca 1 cm wide, tapering, fully attached except for ca 1 mm ligular apex; leaf blade 8–30 by 2–17 cm, very variable in shape, mostly more or less oblong-ovate, occasionally broadly ovate to oblong-lanceolate, base cuneate to obtuse, more rarely truncate to cordate with posterior lobes 0–6 cm long, mid- to very dark green and dull to somewhat glossy adaxially, paler and dull green abaxially, often variegated with a dark green central strip, or bivittate grey-green; midrib somewhat prominent abaxially; primary lateral veins impressed adaxially, prominent abaxially,(6–)10–14 on each side of the midrib, 1.5–3 cm apart; interprimary veins irregular but conspicuous, especially in larger-leaved forms; secondary venation often very inconspicuous; tertiary venation barely visible. Inflorescences (1–)2–several together, with a powerful esteric odour; peduncle mostly hidden within the subtending leaf sheath, to ca 12 cm long; spathe (4.5–)8–18 cm long; lower spathe more or less cylindrical at anthesis, green, (0.4–)1–2.5 cm diam.;spathe limb (incl. terminal mucro) about equalling the lower spathe in length, ivory to pale yellow, inflated to ca 4 cm diam. and turbinate at anthesis, slightly gaping or with the margins loosely overlapping, then abruptly caducous, the interface between the limb and the lower spathe only weakly constricted; spadix (2.5–)6–12 cm long, sessile, cylindrical to distally subclavate; pistillate flower zone about half the length of the spadix, obliquely inserted to adnate for ca ½ its length to the spathe; ovaries more or less flask-shaped, ca 1 mm tall; stigma sessile, button-like; interpistillar staminodes scattered, narrowly stalked and clavate-headed, about twice the height of the pistils, sometimes also crowded at the interface between the female and sterile zones; sterile zone between pistillate and staminate flower zones abruptly but slightly thicker than distal part of pistillate zone, cylindrical, somewhat shorter than (then hidden within lower spathe) to somewhat exceeding (then distally exposed from mouth of lower spathe, rarely completely exserted) the staminate zone, composed of columnar, flat-topped staminodes markedly dissimilar to interpistillar ones; staminate flower zone cylindrical with the apex rounded, to somewhat clavate, ca (0.3–)0.7–1 cm diam.; stamens more or less rectangular to dumbbell-shaped from above (connective reaching anther apex in the former, not in the latter), ca 0.7 mm across, the thecae impressed apically, the rims interrupted laterally by a narrow slit; appendix absent or reduced to a small cluster of columnar staminodes at the summit of the male zone apex. Fruiting spathe very narrowly urceolate to subcylindrical, to ca 5 cm long.

description: Small to very large, slender to very robust, evergreen, scandent, climbing secondary hemiepiphytes, or perching epiphytes with abundant trichosclereids. Stem root-climbing or less often prostrate, often producing long flagelliform shoots with reduced cataphylls and abundant, dimorphic, clasping and feeding roots. Leaves several to many, distichous to spiro-distichous and often forming tufts at the tips of active shoots, juvenile sometimes in a shingl form; petiole mostly channelled, pulvinate apically; petiolar sheath usually broad, persistent or marcescent, occasionally decomposing into a persistent net-like fibrous mass with abundant, stinging sclereids; leaf blade entire, lanceolate, elliptic or ovate to obovate, acuminate, often variegated when juvenile; primary lateral veins either hardly or well differentiated, pinnate, running into marginal vein, secondaries and also sometimes tertiaries parallel-pinnate, higher order venation inconspicuous, transverse-reticulate. Inflorescence very often solitary; peduncle shorter than petiole; spathe boat-shaped, only slightly gaping at anthesis, or opening almost flat, sometimes grossly thickened, caducous to deciduous or persistent or marcescent; spadix sessile to shortly stipitate, cylindrical, narrowly ellipsoid or clavate, shorter than spathe; flowers bisexual, perigone absent; stamens 4, free; filaments oblong, flattened, broad, connective slender; thecae oblong-ellipsoid, dehiscing by apical slits; gynoecium compressed ± rhombo-cylindrical, 1-locular; ovules 1(–2), anatropous, funicle short, placenta basal; stylar region well-developed, prismatic, truncate or with shortly conical central projection supporting stigma; stigma globose, elongate-globose, elliptic, linear, or punctiform. Infructescence a monsterocarp with stylar region deciduous at maturity, ripening dull orange to dull red or white; ovary 1-seeded. Seed rounded, subreniform, compressed, testa thickish, sparsely verruculose or smooth, embryo curved, endosperm present.</br></br>A small genus of secondary hemiepiphytes, or perching epiphytes, rarely scandent shrubs. Leaf blades of juvenile forms, especially the larger-growing species, are often strikingly different in appearance to the adults, not least in the presence of leaf variegation.</br></br>Approximately 30 species distributed from the tropical eastern Himalaya throughout tropical Asia to Australia (Queensland); four species in Thailand (but see note below), none endemic. The common and widespread Sundaic Scindapsus pictus Hassk. and S. treubii Engl. have yet to be recorded from Thailand despite being common species to the south across the Malaysian border with Peninsular Thailand. They are included in the key for the sake of utility but omitted from the species descriptions.

description: Large to gigantic root-climber to 30 m. Stem 10–35 mm diam. Leaves evenly distributed but lower leaves often falling and then leaves tending to become clustered towards stem apices; petiole canaliculate, 33–62.5 cm by 6–20 mm, dark green, smooth, apical pulvinus 20–25 by 5–12 mm, basal pulvinus 2–4 cm by 7–15 mm; petiolar sheath extending to half way along apical pulvinus, at first sub-membranaceous, soon drying scarious, later breaking into regular sections and falling to leave a somewhat roughened, mid-brown scar; leaf blade oblong-elliptic, 45–100 by 25–48 cm, very stiffly coriaceous, matte green adaxially, slightly glaucous abaxially, apex acute to slightly acuminate, base shallowly and narrowly cordate; primary lateral veins parallel, barely or not differentiated from interprimary veins; interprimary veins very numerous, prominent, remaining parallel to primary vein. Inflorescence solitary on the tips of clinging shoots; peduncle 5–8 cm by 4–10 mm; spathe canoe-shaped, 28–33.5 by 11–14 cm when pressed flat, shortly but stoutly tapering, gaping at anthesis and then caducous before anthesis is complete, exterior green, interior yellow at anthesis; spadix cylindrical, 26–28.5 by 3–4.5 cm, sessile, bluntly tapering towards the apex, dull yellow; stylar region 4–10 by 1.5–4 mm, acroscopic-trapezoid, robust, apex flattened; stigma 0.8–3 by 0.1–0.5 mm, transverse-linear. Infructescence light-green, stylar region greatly enlarged and recurved along the margins, waxy-looking, ripening yellow.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Medium to large, moderate to rather robust, semipachycaul, homeophyllous secondary hemiepiphyte to 10 m. Stems terete, ca 1.5–2 cm diam., smooth with pale green epidermis when fresh, drying with epidermis orange-brown and flaking easily. Leaves tending to cluster at tips of shoots; petiole prominently winged, 10–17 by 1–3 cm, apical and basal pulvini weakly defined; petiolar sheath very prominent, spreading and wing-like, persistent, briefly ligulate apically; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate to ovate-elliptic, 14–25 by 8–18 cm, slightly oblique, base rounded and very briefly cuneate, usually oblique, apex acute to attenuate, with a prominent apiculate tubule, dull pale to medium green, juvenile leaves occasionally with irregular, jagged, silvery streaks; midrib raised abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary lateral veins pinnate, slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries and only slightly less prominent, very slightly raised abaxially and adaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± obscure in fresh material, visible as a faint reticulum in dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf, arising on free lateral and less often adherent shoots; peduncle compressed-cylindrical, 9–14 by 1–1.5 cm; spathe broadly cigar-shaped, 11–16 by 3–5 cm, stoutly long-beaked, thinly stiff-fleshy, dull yellow, paler internally, caducous at pistillate anthesis; spadix cylindrical, 6–11 by 1–2.5 cm, sessile, inserted ± level on peduncle; stylar region mostly longitudinally rhombohexagonal, 4–6 by 2–3 mm, truncate; stigma longitudinally elongated, ca 3 mm. Infructescence stoutly fusiform cylindrical, 12–15 by 2–3 cm, stylar plates each with their edges recurving, somewhat waxy in appearance; stigma longitudinally annulate; fruits yellow when ripe with stylar plates sloughing away to reveal red pulp cavities.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Medium-sized, moderately robust, leptocaulous, homeophyllous, scandent secondary hemiepiphyte to 2 m. Stems terete, 1–1.5 cm diam., smooth, bright green when fresh, drying dark brown; stilt-roots stout, arising at each node. Leaves scattered; petiole 10–17 by 0.3–1 cm, apical and basal pulvini defined; petiolar sheath prominent, reaching to the base of the apical pulvinus, persistent; leaf blade ovate-lanceolate to ovate-elliptic, 10–16 by 4–12 cm, very stiffly coriaceous, base rounded, apex acute, with a prominent apiculate tubule, glossy green when fresh, drying dull orange-brown; midrib raised sharply abaxially, slightly sunken adaxially; primary venation pinnate, slightly raised abaxially; interprimaries parallel to primaries and only slightly less prominent, slightly raised abaxially; secondary and tertiary venation ± obscure in fresh material and dried specimens. Inflorescence solitary, subtended by a fully developed foliage leaf, arising on a free lateral shoot; peduncle cylindrical, 6–12 by 0.3–0.4 cm; spathe ellipsoid-cigar-shaped, 6–11 by 3–3.5 cm, stoutly long-beaked, thinly stiff-fleshy, deep yellow, late-caducous; spadix fusiform-cylindrical, 5–8 by ca 1 cm, sessile, tapering markedly basally, inserted ± level on peduncle, white. Fruits not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Small to robust, usually evergreen, sometimes seasonally dormant, monoecious herbs. Stem epigeal, stout, erect or creeping, covered with fibrous remains of leaves and cataphylls. Leaves solitary or few to several together; petiole terete, sheath very short; leaf blade peltate, ovate or ovate-oblong, acuminate, emarginate basally, sinus very shallow, posterior lobes almost absent, membranaceous; basal ribs short, well-developed; primary lateral veins pinnate, forming submarginal collective vein very near margin, marginal vein also present; secondary and tertiary laterals arising from the primaries at a wide angle, then arching towards leaf margin and forming ± conspicuous interprimary collecting vein (‘colocasioid’ venation); higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle shorter than petiole; spathe ovate or ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, not constricted, barely convolute at base, ± fully expanded at anthesis, lower part persistent to fruiting stage, upper part becoming reflexed and revolute, marcescent, yellow or ± dark purple within; spadix much shorter than spathe; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, often longer than staminate flower zone, mostly adnate to spathe; pistillate flowers with gynoecium surrounded by whorl of 2–5, short, staminodes claviform, more rarely staminodes absent; ovary subglobose to ovoid, 1-locular; ovules numerous, hemiorthotropous, funicle distinct, placentae 2–5, parietal, in basal part only or extending from base to apex; stylar region ± lacking; stigma strongly 2–5-lobed; staminate flower zone contiguous with pistillate, cylindrical, ellipsoid or subglobose, fertile to apex, obtuse; synandria 3–6-androus, strongly lobed, apically truncate, synconnective relatively small, impressed at apex; thecae oblong, contiguous, dehiscing by apical pore. Fruit an ovoid berry, many-seeded. Seed ovoid to ellipsoid, testa costate, embryo axile, short, conoid, endosperm copious.</br></br>A genus of about 10 species of small to moderately large, rhizomatous or creeping, mesophytic herbs with creeping to semi-erect rhizomes with conspicuous netted fibres, peltate leaves and large, brightly coloured inflorescences, the spathe reflexing early during anthesis.</br></br>Remarkably, given that the genus is one of the most horticulturally desirable in Asia, the taxonomic status of Steudnera is far from fully resolved and the names applied here must be regarded as provisional. Three distinct species are definitely present in Thailand, although each known from a single collection, with one (here called S. colocasiifolia) known only from a single living plant. The Flora of China account lists an additional two species (S. griffithii (Schott) Schott and S. henryana Engl.) which have not yet been recorded in Thailand, although a sterile collection [K.Larsen & B.Hansen 1730 (BKF)] may be referable to S. henryana.</br></br>All known Thai Steudnera collections are from relatively well-botanized areas in the north. Furthermore Steudnera species are striking and not easily overlooked even when sterile; it thus seems probable that Steudnera species are genuinely rare in Thailand.

description: Medium sized, evergreen herb. Stem rhizomatous, epigeal, erect, later decumbent with age, 20–50 by 1.5–2.5 cm, moderately covered with tattered cataphyll and leaf remains, older portions naked. Leaves several together at the shoot tips; petioles terete, 15–25 cm by 3–5 mm diam., pale green; petiolar sheath very short; leaf blade peltate, ovate, 15–30 by 8–20 cm, apex acute, membranaceous, slightly glaucous medium green adaxially, epidermis hydrophobic, abaxially paler green and often purple-suffused with the veins pale green. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle 15–20 cm, terete, pale green; spathe 15–18 by 8–10 cm, broadly ovate-lanceolate, long acuminate, reflexing on opening, upper part soon withering, marcescent, lower part persistent into fruiting; spathe limb exterior dull brownish yellow, suffused dull red, interior dull yellow, with the red colour suffusing much of the spathe, giving the whole a dull orange appearance, red-purple at base internally, externally somewhat greenish red; spadix 4–7 cm by 4–7 mm; pistillateflower zone cylindrical, dorsally adnate to spathe, pale creamy white; ovary subglobose, 2–3 by 0.5–1 mm, surrounded by a whorl of 5–8 clavate staminodes; style very short; stigma 3–5-lobed, lobes ascending, blunt, not exceeding the style; staminate flower zone oblong-cylindrical, ivory; synandria 4–6-androus, 1–2 by 1.5–2.5 mm, somewhat rounded stellate-polygonal. Infructescence not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Medium sized to robust, evergreen herb. Stem rhizomatous, epigeal, erect, later decumbent with age, 2–40 by 1.5–3 cm, densely covered with tattered cataphyll and leaf remains, older portions eventually naked. Leaves solitary to three together at the shoot tips; petioles terete, 10–18 cm by 3–7 mm diam., pale green; petiolar sheath very short; leaf blade peltate, ovate, 15–30 by 8–18 cm, apex acuminate, emarginate basally, sinus very shallow, posterior lobes almost absent, membranaceous, glossy deep olive-green adaxially, much paler green abaxially. Inflorescence solitary; peduncle 6–12 cm, terete, pale green; spathe 10–14 by 3–5 cm wide, ovate-lanceolate, long acuminate, reflexing on opening, upper part soon withering, marcescent, lower part persistent into fruiting, exterior pale yellow, interior dark yellow, red-purple at base; spadix 4–6 cm by 4–7 mm; pistillate flower zone very weakly obconical-cylindrical, dorsally adnate to spathe, pale creamy white; ovary subglobose, 2–3 by 0.5–1 mm, surrounded by a whorl of 5–8 clavate staminodes; style very short; stigma 3–5-lobed, exceeding style width; staminate flower zone clavate, lilac; synandria 4–6-androus, 1–2 by 1.5–2.5 mm, polygonal-stellate. Infructescence consisting of few to many berries partially covered by the persistentspathe base; fruits ovoid, 6–11 by 4–7 mm diam., ripening dull red.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Medium sized to robust, evergreen herb. Stem rhizomatous, epigeal, erect later decumbent with age, 2–40 by 1–1.5 cm, densely covered with tattered cataphyll and leaf remains, older portions eventually naked. Leaves solitary to several together at the shoot tips; petioles terete 35–40 cm by 3–7 mm diam., pale green; petiolar sheath very short; leaf blade peltate, ovate, 10–35 by 8–14 cm, apex cuspidate, medium to deep olive-green adaxially, strongly glaucous abaxially. Inflorescence solitary, very strongly fragrant of naphtha; peduncle 6–12 cm, terete, mid-green; spathe elliptic lanceolate, 9–10 by 2–5 cm, long acuminate, reflexing on opening, upper part soon withering, marcescent, lower part persistent into fruiting, exterior deep yellow, interior deep purple; spadix 2.5 cm by 5 mm; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, dorsally adnate to spathe, pale creamy white; ovary subglobose, 2–3 by 0.5–1 mm; style very short; stigma 4-lobed, exceeding style width, style and stigma tinged purple; staminate flower zone clavate, free, pale creamy white; synandria, 4–6-androus, 1–2 by 1.5–2.5 mm, 10–16-lobed, shortly stipitate. Infructescence consisting of few to many berries partially covered by the persistent spathe base; fruit ovoid, 6–11 by 4–7 mm diam., ripening dull red.

description: Very small to medium-sized, seasonally dormant or evergreen, glabrous, rarely pubescent or glandular-pubescent, monoecious herbs. Stem a globose, subglobose or irregular tuber, sometimes rhizomatous or stoloniferous, rarely an epigeal stem. Leaves few to several together; petiole D-shaped to terete, apex and middle portion sometimes tuberculate, sheath rather short; leaf blade usually cordate-sagittate, sagittate to hastate, trifid, pedatifid or pedatisect, rarely linear, narrowly lanceolate, elliptico-oblong or cordate, apex rarely tuberculate; primary lateral veins pinnate, forming submarginal collective vein, 1–2 marginal veins also present; higher order venation reticulate. Inflorescence solitary, appearing with or without or after the leaves; peduncle shorter than petiole, often partially to wholly hypogeal; spathe variably constricted between lower part and limb; lower part with convolute margins, persistent or rarely evanescent; spathe limb eventually bending backwards to become strongly revolute or even strongly, circinnately recoiled, broadly ovate to lanceolate, ± acuminate; spadix sessile, shorter, subequal or much longer than spathe; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, subconical to subglobose, separated from staminate flower zone by a rather long axis covered either entirely or only in basal part with staminodes of various shapes, rarely with staminodes above staminate flowers; pistillate flowers with gynoecia orientated horizontally or vertically; ovary ovoid, ellipsoid or obovoid, free, rarely syncarpic, unilocular, ovules 1–3, orthotropous, funicle short, placenta basal; stigma sessile, discoid-hemispherical; staminodes either all similar or diverse in the same spadix, capitate, clavate to spathulate, cylindrical, filiform, subulate or globose, rarely stout and flattened at the tip, or branched, or reduced to verrucae, straight to flexuose, suberect, spreading or decurved; staminate flower zone cylindrical to ellipsoid, usually densely but rarely sparsely flowered; staminate flowers 1–3-androus but usually 1-androus, free, stamens free or sometimes ± connate, anthers subsessile, connective slender, sometimes prominulent; thecae ovoid to ellipsoid, dehiscing by pores or lateral slits extending to the middle or nearly to the base and confluent apically; appendix usually shortly stipitate, rarely with disc-like extension at the base or sessile, smooth, conoid to extremely slender and filiform-subulate, usually long-exserted. Fruit an ovoid berry, 1- or rarely 2-seeded, orange-red, green or white when ripe. Seed globose to obnapiform, testa thin, rugulose to smooth, strophiolate; embryo axile, elongate, straight, endosperm copious.</br></br>About 100 species distributed from E Himalaya and throughout tropical and subtropical Asia as far east as New Guinea & Australia.</br></br>Thirty-two species are recognized in Thailand, 24 of them (75%) endemic. Five undescribed species are included in the key below, bringing the total to 37 but the true number is without doubt far greater.</br></br>Typhonium sensu lato (see, e.g. Hetterscheid & Boyce, 2000) has recently been investigated at the molecular level and a new taxonomy of it has been published by Cusimano et al., (Taxon 59(2): 439–447. 2010). Whereas Hetterscheid & Boyce (2000) based their decision to sink Sauromatum in Typhonium exclusively on morphological analysis, the molecular data and analysis by Cusimano et al., show a well-separated Sauromatum clade which cannot be maintained in Typhonium. The Sauromatum clade contains six species, of which three occur in Thailand. The Australian members of Typhonium s.l. will also be separated from Typhonium as Lazarum A.Hay.

description: Seasonally dormant herb 10–12 cm tall. Stem short, tuberous, globose or ovoid, 10–15 mm diam. description: Seasonally dormant herb to ca 20 cm. Stem short, depressed, tuberous rhizome, ca 3 by 2.5 by 1.5 cm high. Leaves few together; petiole 20 cm by 2 mm, dark purple, upper part fading to pale green, surface with longitudinal rows of elongate, very short, hair-like cells, giving a velvety appearance; leaf blade sagittate, 12 by 4 cm at the middle, anterior part 6 cm long, posterior lobes 6 by 2 cm, apex acute, upper surface green, lower surface pale grey-green. description: Seasonally dormant herb, 10–20 cm tall. Stem a short tuberous rhizome, 2 cm long, producing annual offsets. description: Small, seasonally dormant herb to ca 20 cm tall. Stem short tuberous rhizome, 1.5–2 by 1–1.5 cm. Leaves few together; petiole 17–22 by 2–3 mm, smooth, basal part pale brown with darker brown striations or pale green with pale brownish striations, upper part uniformly bright pale green; leaf blade deeply sagittate, 13–20 cm long, anterior segment lanceolate, 7–11 by 1–2 cm at the base, gradually narrowing to the acute apex, posterior segments parallel or diverging at a rather shallow angle, linear-lanceolate, 6–10 cm by 8–15 mm at the base, acute. Inflorescence emerging alongside the first developed leaf and then again later in the season; peduncle hardly or half exposed or almost entirely exposed, 2–4 cm by 3mm, white with thin reddish purple striations; spathe 4–6 cm long, constricted between the lower part and spathe limb; lower part elliptic-ovate, 1.3–1.8 by 0.9–1.2 cm, exterior veins whitish, in between flushes of brown and irregularly angular to subrectangular dark brown spots and punctuations, or whitish green with pale greenish greyish striations and spots, interior glossy, dirty pale brownish with spots from the exterior shining through, or nearly entirely off-white or pale green; description: Seasonally dormant herb, 2–10 cm tall. Stem a short creeping rhizome. description: Small, seasonally dormant herb to ca 20 cm tall. Stem a short, slightly depressed, tuberous rhizome, ca 3 by 2.5 by 2 cm high, occasionally branching. description: Small, seasonally dormant herb to 30 cm tall. Stem a short, tuberous rhizome ca 3 by 2 cm. description: Seasonally dormant herb, 10–15 cm tall. description: Seasonally dormant herb, 5–40 cm tall. description: Seasonally dormant herb, 10–22 cm tall. Stem a small, short, tuberous rhizome, ca 2 by 1 cm. Leaves few together; petiole 7–20 cm by 1–3 mm, smooth, all green or the base with scattered or numerous, narrow, short, pale or dark reddish brown stripes; leaf blade orbicular (smallest leaves), cordate, triangular-cordate or elongate ovate, acute with a very short apiculum, ca 4–11 by 3–5 cm, basal lobes short, shortly overlapping to slightly divergent, rounded, adaxially green with a greyish flush, abaxially pale green with lower half of midrib quite strongly raised. Inflorescence developing after ca 3 leaves; peduncle subterranean, ca 10 by 2 mm, white; spathe linear, 11 cm long, lower spathe and limb separated by strong constriction, lower spathe and lower part of limb convolute; lower spathe ovoid, ca 10 by 7 mm, exterior dirty white, minutely brownish red punctate, slightly glossy, interior off white, clouded dirty reddish brown near constriction and slightly reddish punctate near the base; spathe limb 10 cm long, basal part (ca 15 mm) convolute (containing the staminate flower zone), elliptic, upper part linear, acute, ca 5 mm broad, slightly twisted and bending sideways, back of upper ¾ keeled, exterior dirty whitish with a very faint greenish or pale brownish hue, sometimes with scattered, short, narrow, reddish brown stripes, interior dirty whitish with a faint dirty greenish hue; spadix longer than spathe, ca 13 cm long; pistillate flower zone shortly conical, 1.5 by 4 mm, flowers congested; ovaries elongate, ca 1.5 by 0.7–1 mm, angular, lower part whitish minutely reddish punctate, upper part with a dirty greenish hue; stigma depressed, very thin, sessile, rounded or oval, dirty reddish brown with a pale green centre or pinkish; sterile interstice above pistillate flower zone with the basal 2 mm staminodial, the remaining 5 mm naked, filiform, white; staminodes narrowly fusiform, 1.5–2.5 by ca 0.5 mm, most sickle-shaped, slightly flexuous, acute, base slightly expanded, white; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 4 by 2.5 mm, flowers congested; stamens ca 1 mm diam., ca 0.5 mm long; anthers very pale pink; appendix filiform, acute, bending sideways, ca 12 cm long, lower part slightly fusiform, ca 2 mm diam., rest ca 1 mm diam., lower part very pale greenish, rest pale brown. Fruit not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium griseum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 310. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 4–15 cm tall. Stem a short tuberous rhizome, ca 1 cm long. Leaves few together; petiole 3–12 cm long; leaf blade ovate, to 7 by 4 cm, base cordate, apex acute; peduncle 15 by 2 mm, white; spathe 6 cm long; lower part ovoid, 7 by 5 mm, outside whitish with brownish pinkish spots lined between the veins; spathe limb 7 mm diam., basal part convolute, apex acute, outside whitish with pale olive-green spots lined between the veins, inside likewise, somewhat transparent; spadix shorter than spathe, 4.5 cm long; pistillate flower zone conical, 2 by 3 mm at the base, 1.5 mm at the apex, flowers congested; ovaries elongate, angular, ca 2 by 1 mm diam., unilocular, uniovulate, transparent white, pale green near the top; stigma sessile, discoid, circular, with a shallow central depression, ca 0.2 by ca 1 mm, very pale pink, surface minutely verruculate; sterile interstice 4 mm long, lower part with staminodes; staminodes ca 2 by ca 0.3–0.4 mm, at first horizontal, then curving upwards, white, terete, slightly obconical or slightly clavate, apex sometimes flattened; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 5 by 2 mm, flowers congested; appendix 3.5 cm long, lower 3 mm narrowed and stipe-like, 1 mm diam., whitish, rest 1.5 mm diam., pale brown, apex obtuse. Fruits not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium laoticum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 311. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Small, seasonally dormant herb to 20 cm tall. Stem a short, depressed, tuberous rhizome, ca 4 by 3 by 1 cm high; Leaves 2–3 together; petiole to 16 cm by 3 mm, surface densely set with short hairs making the surface appear velvety; leaf blade broadly triangular, ca 10 by 14 cm, both surfaces with short hairs, denser on the abaxial surface, especially on the main veins, margin minutely ciliate. Inflorescence appearing after leaves; peduncle subterranean, 8 by 2 mm, white, or minutely spotted reddish pink; spathe 4.5–5 cm long, strongly constricted between lower part and spathe limb; lower part ovoid, 1.8–2 by 1.2–1.5 cm, exterior lower part whitish or dirty whitish, upwards flushed pinkish or purplish brown, near the constriction dirty brownish, interior whitish with a faint greenish flush; spathe limb orbicular, 2.7–3 by 3 cm, deeply boat-shaped, not flattening at anthesis and only half opening, slightly transparent, exterior dirty whitish greenish with a dense pinkish brownish or brownish mottling, interior dull dirty pale olive-greenish or dirty brownish; spadix slightly shorter than spathe, ca 4 cm long; sessile; pistillate flower zone conical, 3 by 6 mm, flowers congested; ovaries elongate, tapering to the base, ca 1.5 by 0.8–1 mm, angular, top truncate, basal half white, upper part spotted reddish pink; stigma sessile, depressed, 0.6–0.8 by 0.2–0.3 mm, surface with numerous transparent hair-like papillae, reddish pink; sterile interstice ca 1.4 cm long, lower part densely covered with staminodes, upper part smooth, white; staminodes subulate, vermiform, acute, the upper ones straight, the lower ones variously curved, mostly downwards, 4—6 mm long, acute, pale yellow or cream; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 10 by 4 mm, flowers congested; appendix elongate conical, 1 cm by 3 mm, short stipitate, base truncate, apex somewhat acute, surface smooth, reddish brown; stipe ca 1.5 mm. Fruit not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium medusae . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 311. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 3–10 cm tall. Stem a short, tuberous rhizome, ca 2 by 1 cm. Leaves few together; petiole 3–7 cm by 2 mm, whitish green, smooth; leaf blade orbicular, 4–7 by 4–6.5 cm, base cordate, obtuse, adaxially slightly bluish green, abaxially pale green. Inflorescence appearing after the leaves; peduncle 5–10 by 2 mm subterranean, whitish; spathe 4–6 cm long, lower part and spathe limb separated by a strong constriction with a very strongly thickened inner wall; lower part ellipsoid-ovoid, 1–1.5 cm by 6–8 mm, exterior and interior glossy whitish with a few pale reddish pink striations; spathe limb erect, 4.4–5 cm, partly convolute basally, remainder concave, apex obtuse, minutely apiculate, exterior and interior whitish with a faint greenish flush; spadix longer than spathe, 7–11.5 cm; pistillate flower zone conical, 1–2 by 3 mm, flowers congested; ovaries elongate; stigma as broad as ovary, with a shallow central depression, verruculate, very pale pinkish; sterile interstice 8–13 mm long, clothed with staminodes to nearly halfway up, the lower part with the staminodes grooved; staminodes very short, slightly clavate, 1–2.5 by 0.6 mm, off-white; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 9–10 by 3–2 mm, flowers congested; stamens white, opening with lateral pores/slits; appendix myosuroid, terete, 5–8 cm by ca 1.2 mm, narrowly acute, base truncate, sessile, cream. Fruit not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium orbifolium . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 312. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Small, seasonally dormant herb to 30 cm tall. Stem a short rhizome, ca 4 by 2 cm, offsetting more or less freely. Leaves several together; petiole smooth, terete, to 30 cm by 5 mm, basal part reddish brown, remainder green; leaf blade smooth, entire and reniform in juvenile leaves, 5–7-pedatifid in adult leaves, 3–20 cm diam., anterior lobe oval, elongate-elliptic or lanceolate, 7–13 by 1–6 cm, subacute to acute, lateral lobes elliptic to lanceolate. Inflorescence appearing after the leaves, long pedunculate; peduncle stout, terete, to 25 cm by 8 mm, spreading on the soil surface, coloured as petiole; spathe 15–25 cm long; lower part ellipsoid-ovoid, 3–4 by 1.5–2 cm, exterior pale green, interior dark maroon, the ventral side flushed with green, the basal part glossy; spathe limb spreading on the soil surface, separated from the lower part by a thick-walled constriction just below the base of the staminate flower zone, elliptic-oval, 14–19 by 8–14 cm, acute-acuminate, upper half slightly reflexed at pistillate anthesis, exterior reddish purple, interior dark maroon; spadix sessile, shorter than spathe, 12–22 cm long, appendix protruding vertically from the horizontally spread spathe; pistillate flower zone conical, 5–7 by 3–5 mm, flowers congested; ovaries cylindrical, base slightly constricted, ca 1.8 mm long, angular, ovary ca 1.5 by ca 0.7 mm; stigma sessile, depressed, ca 0.9 by ca 0.3 mm high, surface densely papillate-verrucate, centre slightly depressed, trans-lucent pale greyish, margin reddish purple; sterile interstice 2–3.5 cm long, basal 1 cm with slightly distant staminodes, remainder naked, brownish purple or pale green; staminodes cylindrical-clavate, perpendicular to the spadix-axis or flexed downwards, 7–8 by ca 0.8 mm, obtuse, bright pale yellow, producing a transparent fluid on their surfaces at pistillate anthesis; staminate flower zone cylindrical, base slightly constricted, 7–10 by 5–7 mm, flowers congested; stamens 1 by ca 0.8 mm; thecae purple, connectives indistinct but elongate-conical in the uppermost flowers; appendix elongate-conical, thin, stipitate, acute, base truncate, 9–14.5 cm by 5–6 mm, dark maroon, rugulose-verruculose; stipe 1–2 cm long, bending horizontally, maroon. Fruit not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium pedunculatum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 312. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 10–23 cm tall. Stem a tuberous rhizome, ca 1–2 cm diam. Leaves few together; petiole 10–20 cm long, covered with short, glandular hairs; leaf blade hastate-sagittate, 7–14 cm long, anterior part ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 4–8 by 2–4 cm, acute, posterior lobes narrowly oblong to lanceolate, 3–6 by 1.5–3 cm. Inflorescence appearing after the leaves; peduncle 2–4 cm long, subtended by a single cataphyll; spathe 2.7–4 cm long, lower part and spathe limb separated by a constriction; lower part ellipsoid to oblong-ovoid, 7–10 by 5–7 mm; spathe limb triangular-ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 2–3 by 1–1.5 cm, purplish green; spadix erect, slightly shorter than spathe, 2.5–3.5 cm; pistillate flower zone cylindrical, 1.5 by 2 mm, with ca 2–3 rows of flowers; ovaries lageniform, 1 mm long; stigma discoid; sterile interstice 6–10 mm long, lower part covered with staminodes, remainder naked; staminodes 2–3 mm long, spathulate; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 8–10 by 2 mm; anthers oblong, 1.5 mm; thecae opening by apical pores; appendix conical, 7–12 by 1–2 mm, stipitate, base truncate, creamy. Fruit not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium pusillum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 313. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, ca 25 cm tall. Stem a short, tuberous rhizome. Leaves few together; petioles ca 21 cm by 6 mm; leaf blade trilobed to pedatifid, ca 6 cm long; central lobe oval, to ca 5 by 4 cm, acute. Inflorescence appearing after the leaves; peduncle 10–15 cm by ca 5 mm, grooved, green; spathe strongly constricted between lower part and spathe limb, 9–12 cm long; lower part ellipsoid, ca 1 cm., exterior green, interior pale green; spathe limb oval, to 5 cm wide, margins strongly reflexing and remainder strongly folded backwards one or several times, exterior green, interior green, becoming slightly transparent shortly after anthesis; spadix shorter than spathe, 7–9 cm long; pistillate flower zone slightly conical, ca 4 by 5 mm, flowers congested; ovaries elongate, ca 1.5 by 0.6 mm, slightly angular, semitranslucent, pale green; stigma disciform, very thin, broader than ovary, margins of adjacent stigmas slightly overlapping, surface papillate, dirty whitish; staminodes fusiform-clavate, slightly or distinctly upcurved, ca 3 by 1.3 mm, yellow, top obtuse; sterile interstice 1–2 cm long, with staminodes basally, remainder smooth, pale green; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 15–18 by 0.4–0.5 mm, base and apex truncate, flowers congested; stamens ca 1.5 mm, salmon pink; appendix elongate conical, 4–5 cm by 2–3 mm, stipitate, base truncate, top narrowly acute, surface slightly rugulose, bright orange; stipe 2–3 mm. Fruit not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium reflexum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 314. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 10–40 cm tall. Stem a short, subglobose or globose tuberous rhizome. Leaf several together; petiole 10–35 cm long; leaf blade reniform-hastate, triangular in outline, dark green above, yellowish green below, shallowly or deeply 3-lobed, terminal lobe ovate, acuminate, (5–)9–17 by 4–14 cm wide, lateral lobes oblique ovate or long ovate, spreading. Inflorescence appearing after the leaves; peduncle creamy red with dark purple dots, 2–9 cm long; Spathe 8–18 cm long; lower spathe ovoid, 2–3.5 by 1.5 cm, outside whitish or pale green with purple stripes, inside purple; spathe limb ovate-lanceolate, abruptly tapering from below the middle, usually twisted at tip, 6–15 by 5 cm, purplish mixed with dirty green flushes or striae outside, or purple all over, inside deep rich purple; spadix subequalling the spathe; pistillate flower zone 4–5.5 mm long; ovaries ovoid, white or yellowish; stigma purple, unilocular, uniovulate; sterile interstice 1.5–2.2 cm long, lower 5–7 mm densely covered with staminodes, remainder naked; staminodes 8–9 mm long, subcylindrical, yellow or pale yellow, acute, weakly papillose, curved downward; staminate flower zone 7–12 mm long; staminate flowers consisting of 2–3 stamens, yellow; anthers sessile, opening by apical pores; appendix narrowly conical, 12–15 cm long, 3–4 mm diam. at the base, dark purple, base truncate with a pale red stipe of ca 2 mm long. Fruits ovoid or ellipsoid, 1-seeded, pale green at first, white when mature.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium roxburghii . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 314. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 19–35 cm tall. Stem unknown but probably a short tuberous rhizome; petiole slender, 19–30 cm long; leaf blade deeply trilobed, sagittate, lobes linear, anterior lobe slightly shorter than posterior lobes, the latter 5–9 cm long, 3–10 mm wide, acuminate. Inflorescence short pedunculate; spathe 3.5–4.5 cm long, lower spathe and limb separated by a constriction; lower spathe ovoid to elongate-ovoid, 12–15 by 5–7 mm, thick-walled; spathe limb erect, elongate triangular, 25–32 mm long; spadix shorter than spathe, 32–35 mm long; pistillate flower zone 2–4 mm long; ovaries congested, 1.5 mm long; stigma sessile; sterile interstice 13 mm long, base with numerous staminodes, remainder naked; staminodes subulate-filiform, recurved, 3–5 mm long; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 7 by 2 mm, stamens congested; appendix narrowly cylindrical-conical, 8 mm long, stipitate, obtuse, brown. Fruit not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium sagittariifolium . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 315. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 15–35 cm tall. Stem a globose tuber, 1–3 cm diam. Leaves few together; petiole smooth, 15–30 cm long, green; leaf blade deeply trilobed, ca 20 cm long, anterior lobe broadly ovate to narrowly ovate, 8–10 cm long, acute, posterior lobes triangular-ovate, to 10 by 5 cm. Inflorescence appearing after the leaves; peduncle 5 cm long; spathe 5–8 cm long, lower part and spathe limb separated by a constriction, less strikingly so on the ventral side; lower part ellipsoid, 2–3 cm by 8–15 mm, exterior yellowish green; spathe limb triangular-ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 3.5–5 by 1.5–3 cm, acute, erect or slightly oblique, exterior and interior yellowish green; spadix erect, shorter than spathe, 5–6.5 cm long; pistillate flower zone 3 mm long, with ca 2–3 rows of flowers; ovaries perpendicular to the spadix axis, narrowly pyramidal, ca 1.5 cm long; stigma discoid; sterile interstice ca 2–2.5 cm, the lower half densely covered with staminodes, the upper half naked, cream; staminodes subulate, 2–4 mm long, curved in various directions; staminate flower zone 1–1.3 cm long; anthers ovoid, pink, opening with apical pores; appendix conical, 1–1.3 cm long, stipitate, base truncate, apex acute, cream. Fruit not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium saraburiense . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 316. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 5–20 cm tall. Stem a tuberous rhizome, 0.5 by 1 cm; petiole 5–14 cm long, 1 mm diam.; leaf blade broadly ovate, 7–9 by 5–8 cm, base cordate, apex acute to short acuminate; peduncle 6–17 cm long, 0.5 mm diam., glandular hairy; spathe 7–8.5 cm long, lower spathe amd limb separated by a constriction; lower spathe ovate; spathe limb broadly ovate-lanceolate, 5.5–7 by 1.5–2 cm, brownish purple inside; spadix slightly longer than spathe, ca 9 cm long; pistillate flower zone 1 by 1.5 mm; ovaries congested; sterile interstice 1–1.2 cm long, lower 2 mm bearing staminodes, remained naked; staminodes clavate (“capitate” fide Sookchaloem & Murata ), 2 mm long, spreading or slightly decumbent; staminate flower zonecylindrical, 3 mm long; appendix filiform, 6.5 cm long. Fruits not known.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium smitinandii . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 317. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 3–10 cm tall. Stem a short tuberous rhizome, ca 1 by 1 cm. Leaves few together; petiole 3–7 cm by 2 mm, smooth, pale green; leaf blade ovate to elongate, 3–7 by 1.5–3 cm, acute, base with two shallow lobes. Inflorescence appearing after the leaves; peduncle ca 2 cm by 2 mm, entirely subterranean; spathe 10–16 cm long; lower part ovate, 10–15 by 6–10 mm, separated from the limb by a dorsal constriction; spathe limb 9–15 cm long, upper part bent forward and strongly coiling when open, lanceolate, 4–9 mm wide, acute, base exterior pale green with a pale purplish base or with numerous small purple spots throughout, interior pale green with slightly purplish veins, limb exterior whitish green but basal part darker, or flushed with brownish purple, interior as exterior but base more strongly purple; spadix longer than spathe, 15–18.5 cm; pistillate flower zone shortly conical, 2 by 4 mm; ovaries elongate, slightly obconical, ca 1.3 by 0.8 mm, translucent whitish, with an occasional purplish flush; stigma sessile, disciform, ca 0.4 by 0.1 mm, verruculate, transparent, white; sterile interstice 9–13 mm long, lower 2 mm staminodial, rest naked, whitish; staminodes ca 1 by 0.8 mm, subglobose or slightly angular, apex obtuse or slightly truncate, surface minutely verruculate, yellow or orange; staminate flower zone short cylindrical, 4 by 3 mm, flowers congested; anthers 1 by 0.5 mm butterfly-shaped, orange, pores apical, elongate; appendix myosuroid, gradually and slightly narrowing to the base, 13–16 cm by 1–1.5 mm, acute, the basal 1–1.5 cm slightly narrower, whitish green, resembling a stipe, remainder pale yellowish brown or brown. Fruits not known.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium subglobosum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 317. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 27–45 cm tall. Stem a short, tuberous, subglobose or subcylindrical rhizome, producing few annual offsets or splitting up. Leaves several together; petiole 25–40 cm long, green or variously flushed with purple; leaf blade cordate-ovate in outline, usually deeply 3-lobed, rarely 5-lobed, central lobe ovate, acuminate, sometimes mucronate, 10–15 by 6–11 cm, lateral lobes 8–13 cm long. Inflorescence appearing after the leaves; peduncle 5–10 cm long, elongating in fruit; spathe to 30 cm long; lower part convolute, ovoid or ellipsoid, 2.5–3.5 by 1–1.5 cm, constricted at the top, green; spathe limb ovate-lanceolate, acuminate, ca 15 by 5–8 cm, spreading, outside green, inside dark purple to reddish purple; spadix shorter than spathe; pistillate flower zone 7–10 mm long, slightly conical; ovary yellowish green; stigmasessile, disciform, dark or mid purple; sterile interstice 2–3 cm long, lower half densely covered with staminodes, upper half naked; staminodes 7–12 mm long, filiform, strongly curled but mostly directed downwards and obscuring most of the pistillate flower zone; staminate flower zone 1.5–2 cm long; stamens pink; appendix elongate conical, 5–12 cm long, 4–7 mm diam., shortly stipitate, truncate at base, tip acute or subacute, glossy purple or reddish. Infructescence with spathe persisting, later reflexing and occasionally splitting longitudinally to reveal ripe fruits; fruits ellipsoid, at first green with purple spots, white when mature.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium trilobatum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 318. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 5–15 cm tall. Stem a subglobose tuber, 1–2 by 1–2 cm, annually producing several globose offsets. Leaves few together; petiole 4–13 cm by 2–3 mm, smooth, lower part terete, upper surface of the upper part distinctly channelled, pale green throughout; leaf blade elongate-ovate to elongate-elliptic-ovate, 6–15 by 3.3–6 cm, slightly coriaceous, acute, base cuneate or slightly truncate, adaxially greyish green, abaxially pale grey green. Inflorescence opening with leaf still very underdeveloped; peduncle 1.5 cm by 3 mm, smooth, subterranean, white; spathe 22 by 2 cm, basal part and spathe limb separated by constriction; lower part strongly convolute, elliptic-ovoid, 2 by 1.3 cm, exterior glossy off-white with a very faint greenish flush, veins slightly darker, interior off-white; spathe limb lanceolate, base erect then arching backwards to the soil, 20 cm long, apex acute, margins dorsally revolute and touching in the upper part to form a narrow tube, interior dull olive greyish green with a golden sheen and semitranslucent or pale purplish brown, exterior glossy pale greyish with a greenish flush; spadix slightly shorter than spathe, 20 cm long; pistillate flower zone conical, 3 by 4 mm, flowers congested; ovaries cylindrical, angular, 1 by 0.4 mm, white; stigma sessile, disciform, 0.4 mm diam., 0.2 mm high, verrucate-penicillate, white, obscuring the ovary; sterile interstice 1.8 cm long, almost entirely covered with staminodes, only upper 3 mm naked, axis white; staminodes of two main types but with intermediates; lower staminodes short, thick rod-shaped, terete or apex slightly thicker than base (subclavate), subangular, white, 4 by 1.5 mm, base truncate, apex subtruncate or obtuse, upper staminodes triangular, lateral sides strongly compressed, attached broadly lengthwise on the spadix-axis, ca 2 by 3 mm at the base, top acutish or obtuse, white; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 1 cm by 4 mm, top truncate, base slightly attenuate, flowers congested; stamens very pale pinkish, opening by sublateral to lateral slits; appendix filiform, 18.7 cm by 3 mm, tapering to the acute apex, base obliquely subtruncate, surface smooth, very pale brown to yellowish brown at the top. Fruits not known.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium tubispathum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 319. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, cm tall. Stem a short, depressed, tuberous rhizome, 3–5 by 3 by 2 cm high. Leaves few together; petiole 7–23 cm long, 1 mm diam., smooth, pale green; leaf blade broadly triangular, 5–17 by 4–17 cm, more or less distinctly trilobate to subpentalobate or fully pentalobate, lateral lobes asymmetrical, ovate to narrowly elliptic, obtuse, central lobe oval, acute, adaxially green, or only the main veins white, or main veins, lateral veins and part of the secondary veins white, with or without dark blackish purple spots between the primary lateral veins, basal margin sometimes flushed reddish. Inflorescence appearing after the leaves; peduncle emerging laterally from the leaf-shoot, subtended by one visible bract, sturdy, to 4 by 1 cm, dilating upwards, smooth, pale green; spathe 9–17 cm long; lower part ovoid, ca 2.5 by 1.5 cm, thick-walled (ca 2 mm), exterior glossy green; spathe limb horizontal, triangular-ovate, 7–14 by 4–7.5 cm, apex acute, exterior dark green flushed with dirty brown, interior at first a rich deep purple at opening, soon turning dark greenish brown or pale dusky brown; spadix slightly shorter than spathe, erect, 8–13.5 cm long; pistillate flower zone conical, 3–5 by 3–8 mm, flowers congested; ovaries more or less elliptic, 1.5 by 1 mm, pale green; stigma sessile, disciform, 0.2 by 0.8 mm, with a central depression, surface densely papillose, dirty whitish greyish; sterile interstice 1.5–2 cm long, lower 5 mm densely covered with staminodes, remainder smooth, dark rich reddish purple; staminodes subulate, acute, 5–8 by 0.8 mm, pale yellow, the upper ones straight, the rest strongly curved downward, obscuring the entire pistillate flower zone; staminate flower zone cylindrical, 1–1.8 cm long, 5–8 mm diam., slightly laterally compressed, flowers congested; stamens pale pink, connective not or very slightly raised; appendix elongate conical, 4.5–9 by 0.6–1 cm, short stipitate, base truncate, slightly notched, apex obtuse, surface very shallowly rugulose, dark grey; stipe obconical, 5 by 4 mm, white. Fruits not seen.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Typhonium varians . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 2, 2012. Pg. 320. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Seasonally dormant herb, 3–7 cm tall. Stem a short tuberous rhizome, to 1 cm long. Leaves few together; petiole whitish green, to ca 6 cm long, to ca 3 mm diam., usually developing a bulbil at its apex; leaf blade reniform (when very small) to ovate, 1–11 by 1.5–6 cm, basal lobes small, often slightly overlapping, apex acute, texture slightly leathery, upper surface green to dark green, sometimes a little glaucous, primary and secondary veins paler, clearly visible; spathe to 10 cm long; lower part convolute, globose or elliptic, to 10 mm diam., veins raised, apex strongly constricted, outside uniformly whitish green or whitish; spathe limb lanceolate, to ca 9 cm long, 10 mm diam., acute, curving backwards and curling at anthesis, pale green or whitish; spadix nearly as long as spathe, to 9.5 cm long; pistillate flower zone hemispherical, 2–2.5 by 4 mm at the base; ovaries congested, lower ones subperpendicular to the axis, upper ones subparallel to the axis; ovaries obconical, to ca 1.7 by ca 0.8 mm at the apex, angular, whitish green, unilocular, with one basal ovule; stigma sessile, disciform, ca 0.5 mm diam., 0.1 mm high. sterile interstice to ca 1 cm long, lower 3 mm with staminodes, remainder naked, smooth; staminodes perpendicular to the axis, to 1.5 mm long, white, clavate or more terete, base decurrent, apex obtuse or acute; staminate flower zone cylindrical, to 12 by 4 mm, flowers congested; stamens whitish with a very faint yellowish flush; appendix myosuroid, terete with base slightly narrowed, sometimes slightly twisted, to ca 7 cm long, ca 1 mm diam., smooth, white, subacute.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Seasonally dormant herb, to 25 cm tall. Stem a subglobose tuber, 5–10 mm diam. Leaves few together; petiole slender, to 20 cm long, smooth; leaf blade ovate to oblong in outline, pedately dissected into 5–7 lobes of approximately similar size, lobes mostly linear, 10–15 cm by ca 5 mm, acuminate, occasionally elliptic to narrowly elliptic and then 4–6 by 1–1.5 cm, base decurrent. Inflorescence appearing after the leaves; peduncle 1–5 cm; spathe ca 4.5 cm long; lower part half subterranean, ovoid, 1.5 cm by 7 mm; spathe limb ovate-lanceolate, ca 3 cm long, oblique, dusky crimson with darker streaks (fide Kerr); spadix nearly as long as the spathe; pistillate flower zone ca 2 mm long with about 5 rows of flowers; sterile interstice ca 15 mm long, lower 4 mm covered with staminodes, naked above; staminodes filiform, ca 2 mm long, variously curved; staminate flower zone 4 mm long; appendix narrowly conical, 2.5–3 cm long, stipitate, dusky crimson (fide Kerr). Fruits not seen.
